articles.title_orig: Israel election: Exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Israel election: Exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
Israel's election result is too close to call , with Gadi Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Benjamin Natanyahu's camp in two exit polls; a third puts the PM's camp marginally ahead - both have fallen short of a majority
Eisenkot leads the newly formed Yashar party and is the main figure in the "change bloc", a group of opposition parties with the shared goal of ousting  Netanyahu
The exit polls also suggest Netanyahu's Likud party is set to be the biggest single party in the Israeli parliament
Israeli elections can be decided by just a handful of seats and exit polls have been wrong in the past
Official results started being released from midnight local time (22:00 GMT), but counting could take days
What lies ahead is likely to be weeks or months of protracted negotiations between the parties, with numerous options on the table, our reporter in Tel Aviv writes
All 120 seats in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, are up for grabs, but no party has ever won a majority and in the past governments have been made up of coalitions
It is Israel's first legislative election since the Hamas-led attacks on 7 October 2023 - what were the big issues on the campaign trail?
Edited by Chris Graham, with James Landale, Hugo Bachega and Tom Bennett in Israel
New exit poll show a tie between Netanyahu and Eisenkot's blocs.
Israel's Kan 11 and Channel 13 news networks have published updates to their exit polls showing the two rival blocs projected to win 51 seats each.
Channel 12 has also revised its exit poll showing the Eisenkot-led bloc marginally behind on 50, while placing Netanyahu's bloc on 52. Earlier, they showed the anti-Netanyahu bloc slightly ahead of the incumbent prime minister.
The winning bloc needs at least 61 seats in the Knesset to form a majority government.
Official results are starting to trickle through from Israel's Central Electoral Committee with 2.5% of votes counted.
Gabriela Pomeroy Live reporter
Exit polls show record gains and turnout for the Arab parties.
I spoke to one of the activists who campaigned to get out the Arab vote  - 29-year-old Mahdi Kabaha, a lawyer in the mainly Arab northern town of Umm Al-Fahm.
"This is a historic night. Arab society showed up and said it clearly: we are here, and we are part of the decision," he says.
Arab voters make up about a fifth of the Israeli electorate and just over half voted in the last election. Many have been reluctant to vote in the past as they âdonât want to legitimise Israeli institutions," Kabaha says.
He has been promoting voting among the Arab community in order to remove far-right ministers like Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.
One of the biggest issues for Arab voters is crime in Arab areas and a lack of policing.
Kabaha campaigned for Israeli Arabs to come out and vote, telling them they should use their voting power to shape the government. âThere is a big difference between [left-leaning Democrats leader] Yair Golan and Ben Gvir in the government. One wants to
take more land and expel Palestinians, and the other wants to find a solution for
two people,â he adds.
Tom Bennett Reporting from Eisenkot's watch party
Eisenkot addresses supporters at Yashar's party headquarters.
Gadi Eisenkot has just arrived at his partyâs HQ here in Tel Aviv, taking a long walk through the crowd onto stage, surrounded by the candidates from his Yashar Party.
âWe made history,â he says. âThis morning, the people of Israel went to a referendum on the leadership of the coming years. The public decided in favour of change.
"The Israeli public voted against the continuation of Netanyahu's term," he says, to big cheers from the crowd.
âIn an election with such high voter turnout, it would be a mistake to go to additional elections. It is our duty, and my personal responsibility, to do everything to respect the will of the people.â
The national anthem was then played before he took an Israeli flag from the crowd and waved it, before exiting the stage.
The official vote count is starting to come through.
So far 2,670 votes have been tallied, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. That represents almost 0.1% of the total number of votes.
Since the polling stations closed at 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT), reporting has relied on exit poll data â which is not an official count, but rather surveys of voters exiting polling stations conducted by media companies.
While the official tally so far is not a meaningful sample size, it does show the electoral body is starting to report as expected.
The turnout for this year's Israeli general election was 77.7% as of 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT) when polls closed, the country's Central Election Committee has said.
The figure represents 5,695,682 individuals having cast their vote by this time, with the committee saying it is the highest percentage recorded at that time since 1999.
Netanyahu's party being the largest in the Israeli exit polls is a "meaningless consolation prize" compared to the prediction of Gadi Eisenkot's bloc being the biggest group, a leading Israeli commentator has said.
"He's had incredible comebacks before, but for the Netanyahu coalition - this is a very, very bad night," Anshel Pfeffer, the Economist's Israel correspondent, tells BBC News.
When asked if the bloc led by Eisenkot has the best chance of forming a governing coalition according to the exit polls, he responds by saying Netanyahu currently has the least.
Pfeffer says he feels the Likud leader could only make a comeback if he manages to convince centrist parties to join him in a unity government, adding: "I'm not going to put that past him."
The leader of Israel's left-leaning Democrats party has said it is willing to "work with all our partners" and "bridge differences" to form a new government for the country.
Speaking in a post on X following the exit polls, Yair Golan says "the public has spoken" and "ousted the Netanyahu government", adding this is a "historic opportunity to establish a true government of change".
Meanwhile, Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid says in a separate post that Netanyahu's bloc has suffered a crushing defeat.
For context: Official results will start being released from midnight local time (22:00 GMT), but counting could take days.
Gadi Eisenkot is a former head of the Israel Defense Forces, now leading the centrist Yashar party. He has built his campaign on calls for accountability over the security failures that led to 7 October.
His popularity stems partly from his military credentials and his status as a relative political newcomer, having formed his party only last year.
He lost his son, a soldier, in the first months of the Gaza war, and served in Israel's war cabinet under Benjamin Netanyahu until resigning in 2024 over the PM's handling of the conflict.
On Gaza, Eisenkot does not differ hugely from Netanyahu. He recently pledged to end Hamas rule in the territory within 18 months, through a US-led peace plan or, if necessary, military means.
He supports Israeli settlements in general, but opposes proceeding with the controversial E1 settlement project which would, in effect, split the West Bank in two.
Paul Adams Diplomatic correspondent
Reports suggest that a high turnout among Israeli Arab voters has been translated into electoral success, with the two Arab-majority parties (The United Arab List - or Raâam - and The Joint List, an alliance of three smaller parties) projected to win as many as 19 seats between them (which would be a record).
The main parties in Israel have traditionally been extremely reluctant to include Arab parties in their coalitions, but with the gap between the two main electoral blocs projected to be narrow, the Arab-majority parties will be hard for Eisenkot and Netanyahu to ignore.
In past Israeli elections, Arab turnout has generally been lower than Jewish turnout. But this time, the desire to see the back of Netanyahu seems to have driven large numbers of Arabs to the polls. Neta

Confrontations with Chinese troops ‘continuing at multiple locations along the Arunachal Pradesh border’, according to Indian authorities
Shatrujeet Kapur, director general of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), said last week that confrontations with Chinese troops were “continuing at multiple locations along the Arunachal Pradesh border”.
“In the past few days, a situation arose where face-off[s] happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues,” Kapur said at a military ceremony on Thursday, according to Indian daily The Hindu.

articles.title_orig: Israel Election 2026 live updates: Netanyahu, Eisenkot caught in deadlock
articles.title_zh: Israel Election 2026 live updates: Netanyahu, Eisenkot caught in deadlock
articles.content_orig:
Fox News Digital speaks with three experts on Israel’s high-stakes election and the fight over Netanyahu’s political future. The election is set for Oct. 27, 2026.
JERUSALEM — Israel’s high-stakes election on Oct. 27 pits the longest serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, against the highly decorated retired Lt. Gen. Gadi Eisenkot. While fairly new to politics, Eisenkot has an impressive resume that could help him become the Jewish state's next leader.
According to a number of polls, Eisenkot's centrist political party, Yashar, has a narrow lead over Netanyahu's Likud. To form a government, Yashar or Likud will need to cobble together a 61-seat majority of parties to be able to form a new coalition government.
TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, speaks from behind a podium with a banner reading "Yashar with Eisenkot" during an event presenting the party's full candidate list ahead of October's general election on Sept. 7, 2026 in Rosh HaAyin, Israel. Eisenkot, a retired chief of the Israel Defense Forces, has emerged as the foremost challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Erik Marmor/Getty Images)
He was born in Tiberias in Israel’s north to a Jewish-Moroccan family who relocated to Israel’s southernmost city, Eilat, on the Red Sea when he was a toddler.
A career soldier, he opted to serve in the infantry. He was part of the elite Golani Brigade and reached the zenith of the military with his 2015 appointment to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) chief of staff in 2015 until 2019.
Yossi Melman, one of Israel’s most respected journalists on intelligence and defense reporting, told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot, "Is 100% a soldier. He is very brave and humble. He is an officer and gentleman."
Melman noted that when Eisenkot was chosen to be the next IDF chief of staff, he declined because he felt that then General Benny Gantz should receive the appointment. Melman asked, "How many people would do that? He was selected after Gantz. It shows his traits of modesty, honesty and not arrogant."
Melman said, "It is a miracle he is leading in the polls. He is the antithesis of a what a politician should be. He is not a great orator when you compare him to Netanyahu. He radiates honesty."
BENJAMIN NETANYAHU'S LEGACY AND POLITICAL FUTURE ON THE LINE IN ISRAEL'S OCT 27 ELECTION
Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot attends the Jerusalem Residents Conference on Aug. 12, 2026 in Jerusalem. Gadi Eisenkot, a retired chief of the Israel Defense Forces and current leader of the Yashar party, has emerged as the foremost challenger to Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of October's general election. (Erik Marmor/Getty Images)
Eisenkot’s Mizrahi background — Jews who originate from North Africa and the Middle East — would mean, if he prevails, that he would be the first Israeli Prime Minister of Moroccan origin. The Prime Minister’s office has been held by Israelis of Eastern European descent (Ashkenazi) since the rebirth of the Jewish state in 1948.
After Hamas invaded Israel on Oct. 7, 2023 and slaughtered over 1,200 people, including more than 40 Americans, Eisenkot joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet as a minister without portfolio.
Melman said Eisenkot "did not set any political conditions" and "his presence in the cabinet saved Netanyahu." After eight months of serving in the war cabinet, Eisenkot resigned, blaming the prime minister for failing to implement a comprehensive strategy.
The war against the Iran-backed terrorist movement Hamas took an enormous toll on the battle-hardened General Eisenkot and his family. Hamas killed his son, 25-year-old Master Sergeant Gal Eisenkot, in Dec. 2023. The terrorist organization also killed two nephews of Eisenkot. Netanyahu and his wife Sara said at the time that they were devastated by Gal’s death and Eisenkot was a "true hero."
ZIONISM EXPLAINED FROM ITS BIBLICAL ORIGINS TO THE REBIRTH OF THE STATE OF ISRAEL
Gadi Eisenkot, former Israeli army chief of staff and head of the Yashar party, is seen at the Black Arrow memorial site near Kibbutz Mefalsim during a visit to deliver a statement near the border with the Gaza Strip on Oct. 15, 2026, ahead of the Israel's legislative election. (Ilia Yefimovich/AFP via Getty Images)
Danny Orbach, a military historian from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, gave his take on the leading contender to replace Netanyahu. "I think his military record and his prospects as a national leader have both significant strengths and serious weaknesses. He bears considerable responsibility for shaping the IDF that existed on Oct. 7, 2023. And that was, paradoxically, both the army that proved capable of defeating Hezbollah, striking Iran and achieving unprecedented military successes in the extraordinarily difficult, tunnel-ridden battlefield of Gaza and the army that failed so miserably on Oct. 7."
He continued that, "Like other chiefs of staff, Eisenkot bears responsibility for the decisions that reduced the army's size and for the infamous ‘conceptzia’ [Hebrew word for concept] regarding Hamas. In that respect, I consider him just as culpable as Netanyahu."
Israel’s military, intelligence and political establishments bought into the ‘conceptzia’ that Hamas could be housebroken with massive infusions of economic aid. Hamas, however, was wedded to its radical Islamist ideology —the destruction of the Jewish state — and used the funds to advance its war aims.
Orbach noted that "I don't think most of Eisenkot's support stems from his energy, enthusiasm or even his political platform. My impression is that Eisenkot has emerged as the default ‘non-Bibi’ candidate, the politician who currently channels much of the camp's hopes and expectations."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israeli Chief of Staff Gadi Eizenkot (L) give a press conference in Tel Aviv, on Dec. 4, 2018. Israel's army said today it has discovered Hezbollah tunnels infiltrating its territory from Lebanon and launched an operation to destroy them, a move likely to raise tensions with the Iran-backed group. (Jack Guez/AFP Via Getty Images)
Orbach added that "I also doubt that Eisenkot would have had the political determination to stand up to the Biden administration on such matters."
Netanyahu and former President Biden repeatedly clashed over Biden’s attempts to rope in Israel’s efforts to defeat Iran’s seven-front war against the Jewish state.
The military historian, however, noted that "I believe an Eisenkot government could address several of Israel's most urgent problems. It would remove Ben Gvir from power, confront the growing problem of Jewish extremist violence and terrorism in the West Bank, and begin repairing Israel's severely damaged international legitimacy."
Itamar Ben-Gvir is a controversial right-wing firebrand politician and the current minister of national security since 2022, who has outraged many Western European and foreign leaders with his heated rhetoric against the Palestinians.
TIMELINE OF DECADES-LONG ISRAELI-ARAB, PALESTINIAN CONFLICT
Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot attends the funeral for his son, First Sergeant Major Gal Meir Eisenkot, 25 years old, at the Herzliya cemetery on Dec. 8, 2023 in Herzliya, Israel. The Israel Defense Forces said the 25-year-old major, son of the cabinet minister and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, died on Thursday in Gaza. (Dima Vazinovich / Middle East Images / Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images))
Eisenkot’s wife, Hannah, comes from an American Jewish family. U.S. General Joseph Dunford awarded Eisenkot the Commander of the Legion of Merit because of his "exceptionally meritorious service as chief of the General Staff of the IDF" and his "contribution to the strategic cooperation between the United States and Israel [that] will have a lasting effect on both countries," according to the Washington Institute, where Eisenkot served as a military fellow in 2019

articles.title_orig: ‘Awfully bleak’: why global carmakers keep losing ground in China’s vast market
articles.title_zh: ‘Awfully bleak’: why global carmakers keep losing ground in China’s vast market
articles.content_orig:
Carmakers are scrambling to revamp their strategies as China’s cash-strapped consumers turn away from expensive foreign brands
Global carmakers are searching for a way to survive in China’s cutthroat market, as they continue to lose ground to domestic competitors in a landscape that is increasingly tilting towards electric vehicles.
International auto brands from Volkswagen to Toyota saw their market share in the Chinese mainland slide once again in the third quarter of the year, as consumers turned away from expensive foreign cars amid an economic slowdown and the Iran war.
Foreign marques accounted for less than 30 per cent of deliveries over the period, down from 34.6 per cent a year earlier, as they delivered just 1.38 million cars to mainland customers, according to data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).

articles.title_orig: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
articles.title_zh: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
articles.content_orig:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic , which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet , which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon , Broadcom and Google , while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom , which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX , which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark .
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.

articles.title_orig: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.title_zh: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
President Vladimir Putin received a joint call from the leaders of Norway and Finland on Tuesday as they urged him to end the war in Ukraine, sparking rare contact between Europe and Russia.
The aim of the call, initiated by the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, was to look at “future negotiations to help end the war”.
Store said he and Stubb “stressed the importance of de-escalation” as both leaders voiced strong support for Ukraine, speaking to President Volodymyr Zelensky straight after Putin.
Tuesday’s “frank and substantive” 90 minute phone call was conducted from Helsinki, Finland’s capital, and showed “big differences in views”, according to Store
Following the call, Putin said the duration of the conflict , which has been raging on for four years, has been prolonged by “confrontational” EU and NATO policies, and that a “just and lasting peace” would only be possible if Russia’s interests were considered.
Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on how to end the war that began with Russia's invasion in February 2022, and long-range airstrikes by both sides have increased this year while battle lines have remained largely static.
"The discussion (with Putin) was frank and substantive. We are neighbouring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact ⁠on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," Stubb said.
The Kremlin's readout of the call did not suggest any softening of Putin's position.
"It was emphasised that achieving a just and long-term peace is possible only if the legitimate interests of the Russian Federation are fully and unconditionally taken into account," it said.
"At the same time, ⁠attention was drawn to the confrontational policies of EU and NATO countries, which are contributing to the prolongation of the hostilities."
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Tuesday's call had offered nothing new on the `Ukraine conflict, which he said was likely to escalate, and that European countries were simply seeking a role in the negotiation process.
Western European leaders have mostly refused to talk to Putin, hoping to isolate him. But they have been sidelined in peace efforts led by US President Donald Trump, who is seen in many European capitals as unpredictable and prone to side with Putin at Ukraine's expense.
That perception has been reinforced by deals this month in which Putin agreed to supply Russian diesel to the United States and Trump eased sanctions on Russia.
Ukraine has also complained of disruption to intelligence-sharing by the US and to satellite internet services on which its military relies.
Gerhard Mangott, an Austrian political analyst, said European governments had "manoeuvred themselves into a dead end" when it came to finding a solution to the war, and Tuesday's call was an effort to establish a channel for dialogue.
He drew attention to remarks by Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov on Sunday suggesting Europe should be part of discussions. "I interpret this as a shift in Russia's position, given that Moscow had previously consistently rejected the ⁠idea of discussing a settlement of the war in Ukraine with the Europeans," Mangott said.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been coordinated with Kyiv and was "the right approach".
"We welcome such active support for our diplomatic efforts and peace process," he said, adding that he also hoped a local ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky could "pave the way to other steps in the peace process."
But Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she saw no signs that Russia wanted peace, adding: "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo."
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said other European leaders were not informed of the talks . "My impression is that everyone wants peace, except for Putin himself. I have quite low expectations for this type of conversation," Kristersson told Swedish daily DN.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he had told Stubb and Stoere that "absolute caution and vigilance are necessary in such contacts".
Stubb and Stoere said they acted as leaders of their respective countries and not on ‌behalf of Europe, and had "consulted thoroughly with all our partners."
Russia has frequently accused European governments of stoking the war by arming Ukraine and refusing direct talks. A source close to the Kremlin said French President Emmanuel Macron had been the last EU leader to speak with Putin — in a summer call that yielded no results and was not ‌made public.
The source said Putin told Stubb and Stoere that the European involvement was `welcome and that the war needed to end "taking into account the realities on the ground".
Asked what this meant, the person said it signified that Russia would not compromise ⁠over its aim to capture the whole of Ukraine's Donbas region. The Europeans responded by saying a "just" peace was needed, the source said.
The two Nordic leaders may be less encumbered than their peers from larger European states such as Britain, France and Germany, whose ties with Moscow have deteriorated further.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said attempts to end the war "can never find solutions without Ukraine", and must include European countries.
Merz said Germany and other European states wanted to establish a format to speak to Russia's government and that Norway and Finland were playing "a very constructive role" in that effort. The Kremlin said Putin, Stoere and Stubb would keep in touch by phone.

articles.title_orig: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.title_zh: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.content_orig:

articles.title_orig: Mbappe seeks to defuse anger in China after Mao 'dictator' comment
articles.title_zh: Mbappe seeks to defuse anger in China after Mao 'dictator' comment
articles.content_orig:
By WILL HALLOWELL, NEWS REPORTER
Published: 04:53 EDT, 27 October 2026 | Updated: 11:40 EDT, 27 October 2026
Kylian Mbappe has been dropped by Chinese brands while state TV stations have suspended all LaLiga broadcasts following a joke about Mao Zedong.
A video circulated online in which the French Real Madrid superstar apparently mocked the former Chinese Communist Party leader.
In the footage, he said the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photo-shopped onto that of 'some guy – I think he's a Chinese dictator'.
Mbappe has apologised for the 'ill-judged' joke, saying he has 'deep respect' for China and its history.
Meanwhile LaLiga president Javier Medrano has also been forced to weigh in and apologise to China, describing Mbappe's comments as 'offensive' and adding that the Spanish league is 'taking measures... to overcome this situation'.
In China, jokes about Mao – the country's founding leader who died in 1976 – are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.
Mbappe had brand deals with the drinks giant Dongpeng and China's largest dairy producer Mengniu, who have now cut ties with the 27-year-old.
Adverts showing AI-generated images of the France captain drinking a Dongpeng sports drink were regularly shown in China during this year's World Cup.
Chinese brands have dropped French football star Kylian Mbappe after he 'joked' about former leader Mao Zedong
In China, jokes about Mao – the country's founding leader who died in 1976 – are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo
The meme that football fans had created photoshopping Mbappe's face onto Mao, which he references in the video
Those firms have now dropped Mbappe after accusing him of offending the nation.
China Media Group, the state broadcaster, has also reportedly stopped broadcasting LaLiga matches and advertisements involving Mbappe, citing the Frenchman's 'seriously negative conduct' concerning China, according to EFE .
Dongpeng said in a statement: 'Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.'
The drinks giant added that 'with immediate effect we are terminating all co-operation with Kylian Mbappe'.
Mengniu said in a statement: 'With immediate effect our company is terminating all co-operation with Kylian Mbappe.
'Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.'
Until this incident, Mbappe was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.
Mbappe is fondly nicknamed 'Guigui', the Chinese translation of 'Turtle', due to his perceived similarity to one of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
A bus featuring Mbappe for Dongpeng's Bushuila electrolyte drink is seen on a street in Shanghai
Mengniu milk products are seen on a shelf at a store in Beijing. The brand has dropped Mbappe after his 'joke' about Mao
Mbappe seen on bottles of one of Dongpeng's electrolyte drinks
The centre-forward's comments in the video were an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer's face and other historical figures.
In a statement on Tuesday, Mbappe said: 'During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself.
'My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.
'I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention.
'I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history. I am sincerely sorry.'
LaLiga president Mr Medrano said: 'From LaLiga, we deeply regret the statements made by Kylian Mbappe that have caused discomfort and offense in China.
'We understand the harm caused and, on behalf of LaLiga I wish to convey our sincere apologies to the Chinese people.
'For many years, we have built a relationship of respect, trust and co-operation with China, its authorities, its sports institutions, its audiovisual operators, and millions of fans of Spanish football.
'We cannot allow an individual action to tarnish that relationship or harm the more than 20 clubs in our professional competitions and millions of Chinese fans.
'We are taking the measures within our reach and working directly with our partners and interlocutors in China to overcome this situation.
'Our commitment to China, its people, and its institutions is steadfast. A relationship built over so many years cannot be damaged by a single episode.'
Four topics related to Mbappe were still among the top ten trending searches on China's social media platform Weibo on Tuesday morning.
Some users called for China to 'blacklist' Mbappe and reduce his commercial value to zero. These comments received hundreds of likes.
Fans have been creating memes superimposing Mbappe's face on images of military and political leaders to suggest that he has the power to call the shots at the teams he plays for.
In an interview with L'Equipe last month, Mbappe said that while some aspects of the meme trend were harmless fun, the viral ones depicting him as a dictator showed 'a lack of political and human awareness'.
When asked about the incident, a spokesman for China's Foreign Ministry said that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people 'will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society'.
Mbappe has now apologised for the offence caused by his joke, which the France star admitted was 'ill-judged'
'Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe' has been the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo.
One Weibo user said that the 'extremely serious wrong remarks... crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable'.
Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe's image from their energy drink bottles.
Dongqiudi, one of China's biggest online football outlets, said on Monday evening that Mbappe's remarks were 'offensive to China and the Chinese people' and 'have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people'.
Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator, in an interview with French sports newspaper L'Equipe.
He said: 'There's a part of it that's funny. You can tell that, for some people, it's all in good fun.
'But there is another part that's a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history.'
The 27-year-old added: 'Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people – well, I don't think I've ever done anything like that in my life.'
The furore in China came a day after Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d'Or, the most prestigious individual award in football.
Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there.
Former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island's vice president and current president Lai Ching-te, sparking fury on Chinese social media.
Beijing claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.
Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.
Chinese media outlets reacted with fury to Mbappe's comments on Tuesday.
'A remark about an internet meme has triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the limits of celebrity influence,' state media outlet China Daily said.
'What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it,' the state-backed Global Times said.

articles.title_orig: United ‘hijack’ text scare forces plane to turn back
articles.title_zh: United ‘hijack’ text scare forces plane to turn back
articles.content_orig:
LAS VEGAS ( FOX5 ) — A New Jersey man told police he was just bantering with a coworker before a flight was forced to return to Las Vegas due to a “security concern,” according to an arrest report.
Dante Raymond Milne, from Woodridge, New Jersey, was arrested Oct. 25 on a charge of making a threat or false information regarding an act of terrorism, according to the report. Bail was listed at $20,000.
United Airlines Flight 1681 left Harry Reid International Airport on Oct. 24 at about 11 p.m. en route to Newark, New Jersey, according to the report.
MORE ON FOX5: Police detain man accused of making threats of terrorism on flight out of Las Vegas
After departure, the aircraft returned to Las Vegas following the discovery of a text message about hijacking and crashing the aircraft, the report states.
Upon the plane’s return, an officer escorted two passengers off the aircraft. The report states one passenger sat in seat 37D and Milne sat in seat 10C.
The passenger in 37D told the officer he received a text message from Milne that read, “I’m gonna hijack this b---- and crash ur row only,” according to the report.
A United Airlines flight attendant told a detective she observed an incoming message on the 37D passenger’s phone from the passenger in 10C that began with the words “I’m gonna hijack,” according to the report. She identified the message as a potential aircraft security threat and notified the lead flight attendant.
The flight attendant said the crew waited until the aircraft passed 10,000 feet, consistent with flight procedures, before notifying the captain, according to the report. The captain was briefed and cockpit security procedures were followed. The crew did not confront the passenger and maintained a calm cabin, the report states.
After his arrest, Milne told detectives he was in Las Vegas for a three-day apprenticeship training program for his work as an underwater welder, according to the report. He said he drank beer and shots at an airport bar before boarding, intended to sleep during the flight and was awakened to learn the aircraft was returning to Las Vegas.
According to the report, Milne acknowledged exchanging text messages with the other passenger but initially said he could not recall the content. When asked about the hijacking message, he characterized the wording as poorly stated and suggested the conversation was “banter between coworkers”, the report states.
Milne denied intending to hijack the aircraft, crash it or harm anyone, according to the report. The report states he acknowledged the seriousness of the aircraft returning to Las Vegas and expressed remorse.
The FAA has told FOX5 they are also investigating the incident.
Milne was booked into Clark County Detention Center, and has since posted bond on a $20,000 bail. His attorney told a judge Tuesday morning that they plan to plead not guilty.
He is due back in court on Tuesday, Jan. 5.

articles.title_orig: Ex-JPMorgan banker in 'sex slave' suit accused of getting sister to lie about kissing, racial remark: filing
articles.title_zh: Ex-JPMorgan banker in 'sex slave' suit accused of getting sister to lie about kissing, racial remark: filing
articles.content_orig:
The ex-JPMorgan banker who accused his boss of making him her “sex slave” got his sister to lie in sworn testimony for him — claiming she saw the boss kiss her bro on the neck and tell him, “I own you, Brownie” — according to a new filing from the bank that seeks to dismiss the case.
Chirayu Rana allegedly enlisted the help of both his sis and a close friend to back his lurid allegations against Lorna Hajdini — who fired back last month that Rana was actually waging a “deliberate and sustained scheme” to portray her as a racist sexual predator and criminal.
In a Monday night filing in Manhattan federal court, JPMorgan renewed its allegations of lies and misconduct by Rana, saying they deserve “the most serious sanction available.”
The bank said the money man got his sister Chandani Rana and chum Allan Flott to lie in order to bolster his accusations that Hajdini forced him to have sex and demanded submissive behavior in general.
Chandani Rana initially swore to seeing Hajdini kiss her sibling on the neck and saying denigrating words along the lines of,  “I own you, Brownie” — echoing her brother’s allegations of racism.
Chandani Rana took back the remarks earlier this month, saying:  “I have never seen Ms. Hajdini engage in any inappropriate, sexual, harassing, threatening, or intoxicated conduct toward my brother or anyone else.”
Flott previously claimed Hajdini exhorted her to join Chirayu Rana for a threesome in a bedroom at Flott’s place, allegedly saying, “You know, I own Chirayu, so you’d better come join.” JPMorgan said Flott was “led astray” by his friend, though he’s yet to take back the story.
Back in April, Rana accused Hajdini of coercing him into sex and promising career advances in return – including forcing him into oral sex, grabbing his genitals, and threatening to “ruin” him if he didn’t obey.  He also accused the company for racism and creating an environment for sexual harassment.
JPMorgan and Hajdini — who countersued in May, saying the accusations torched her career and damaged her reputation — are demanding Chirayu Rana cover their legal costs.
“No order can fully restore Ms. Hajdini’s reputation ​or undo what she has suffered,” her lawyer Melissa Rodriguez said in a court filing. “But the court can put an end to this fraudulent litigation, hold ​those responsible accountable, and put an end to Ms. Hajdini’s ongoing nightmare.”
Rana has had trouble getting legal representation throughout the case.
His latest lawyer, Jon Norinsberg, has asked to leave the case, pointing to “irreconcilable differences” with Rana. Norinsberg declined to comment to Reuters, citing court instructions.
High-powered attorney Daniel Kaiser quit from repping Rana in May. Yet another lawyer ceased repping the money man during negotiations with JPMorgan before the suit was filed.
Rana left JPMorgan in late 2025 for private equity firm Bregal Sagemount, which cut ties with him in April after less than six months on the job over performance concerns, company insiders previously told The Post.
The Post has sought comment from Norinsberg.

articles.title_orig: China’s top-secret spaceplane can’t hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.title_zh: China’s top-secret spaceplane can’t hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.content_orig:
A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military’s X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.
The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.
Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. A US Space Force official revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference in South Korea, but the Pentagon did not release the full-resolution image to the public until Monday, when it appeared in an unclassified Defense Intelligence Agency assessment of threats to the United States in space.
The DIA report doesn’t reveal much new about what the Chinese spaceplane does in orbit. China has launched four spaceplane missions since 2020 with durations of up to nine months. The fourth mission is in orbit today after launching in February. It is not publicly known whether China has one or more such spaceplanes in its inventory.
The Space Force has two X-37Bs flying in rotation, with the longest of their eight missions to date running two-and-a-half years from launch until landing. US officials have released photos of the X-37B vehicles, published information about their design and dimensions, and disclosed a handful of experiments they have carried into orbit. Most of the X-37B’s activities in space are classified.
Like the X-37B, China’s spaceplane lifts off inside the payload shroud of a conventional rocket, then operates as a satellite once in orbit. The spaceplane flies like a miniature unpiloted version of NASA’s Space Shuttle and reenters the atmosphere for an autonomous land runway landing at the end of each mission. Ground teams then refurbish it for another flight.
The “enhanced maneuverability” of spaceplanes make them “more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,” the DIA said in its report. So far, the Chinese spaceplane has only flown in low-Earth orbit (LEO) at an altitude of a few hundred miles. One of the Space Force’s X-37B flights soared to an altitude of more than 24,000 miles before using aerobraking to set up for reentry and landing .
Spaceplanes like China’s and the X-37B can also deploy small satellites from their cargo bay. Most recently, China demonstrated an ability to catch an object in orbit, perhaps using a robotic arm. The vehicle now in space released a sub-satellite in June and recaptured it in July, then did the same thing again in August and September, according to an analysis of open source orbital tracking data by Jonathan McDowell , an astrophysicist who catalogs spaceflight activity.
The official name of the Chinese spaceplane is even a mystery. It is often called Shenlong in Western publications, citing reports from the 2000s about China’s development of a robotic spaceplane. Chinese state media only refer to the vehicle as Chongfu Shiyong Shiyan Hangtian Qi, or CSSHQ, which means reusable experimental spacecraft, according to a fact sheet published by the Secure World Foundation .
The DIA did not disclose the exact circumstances of Maxar’s observation of the Chinese spaceplane, such as its timing, location, or distance, but Earth observations often use cameras to view other objects in space as their orbits intersect, an emerging field known as non-Earth imaging (NEI).
NEI allows commercial operators and government analysts to inspect satellites. This is especially useful for gleaning information about classified or proprietary satellite designs, extending a new avenue for international and corporate espionage to the high frontier.
The capability exhibited by Maxar and other commercial companies in the NEI field is distinct from the recent actions of some military spacecraft, such as Russia’s Kosmos 2612, which deliberately maneuvered to approach a US-registered radar imaging satellite earlier this month. Commercial NEI observations come from chance encounters, often at extremely high speed.
The DIA’s assessment of space threats includes an update on China’s pursuit of anti-satellite technology, or “counterspace” weapons. The intelligence agency reported the Chinese military likely considers directed-energy weapons (DEWs) “ideal counterspace systems” because they can be used to permanently or temporarily disable a satellite. One potential use for lasers in space would be to dazzle a sensor on an adversary’s satellite.
“China has multiple ground-based laser weapons with varying power levels to disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in LEO,” the DIA said. “By the late 2020s, China may field space-based directed energy systems and higher-powered ground-based directed energy systems capable of threatening satellites in higher orbits.”
The DIA noted China’s testing of ground-based anti-satellite missiles and the country’s historic demonstration last year of satellite refueling in geosynchronous orbit, a regime some 22,000 miles (36,000 kilometers) over the equator, something no other country has achieved above LEO. China has also tested a robotic arm that could snag a spacecraft out of orbit, and now operates a growing fleet of satellites called TJS that routinely approach foreign spacecraft.
The US Space Force also has a constellation of inspector satellites in geosynchronous orbit and recently procured more that could be refueled, overcoming maneuverability limitations. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink revealed last month that the Pentagon has fielded weapons in space , making the United States the first nation to acknowledge possession of orbital weapons.
Russia is pursuing its own orbital combat program, which includes an ambition to deploy a nuclear weapon in space, according to US intelligence officials.
A more conventional Russian weapons system, known as Nivelir, is designed to fire projectiles from one satellite to smash into another. The Russian military simulated an attack using the Nivelir system in 2020. In April, Russia launched a fleet of small satellites into an orbit close to a commercial radar remote sensing satellite owned by ICEYE that provides reconnaissance imagery to Ukraine. One of the Russian satellites moved within “tens of meters” of the ICEYE satellite earlier this month before backing away, US officials said.

Apple introduces :br(s):the new 14‑inch :br(s):MacBook Pro with M6
Supercharged by M6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features incredible performance and next-level AI capabilities, enhanced connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life, delivering even more value
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.
“The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities
M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.
The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables : 3
A Huge Upgrade with Even More Value
There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.

articles.title_orig: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
articles.title_zh: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
articles.content_orig:
A Delaware proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents would help the firms’ human owners evade legal responsibility for reckless and harmful actions taken by the AI, US Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) told Delaware Governor Matt Meyer in a letter yesterday.
Comer, chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told Meyer that the committee “seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).”
Comer said the proposal is ripe for abuse. “We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives,” Comer’s letter said.
Comer suggested he may propose a federal law that would limit states’ regulatory authority. He said the committee’s probe of Delaware’s plan would “inform possible federal legislative efforts including proposals to appropriately limit state AI regulatory initiatives.” Citing the Oversight Committee’s “jurisdiction to study intergovernmental relationships including those of states,” Comer asked for documents related to development of the proposal and potential AI safety risks.
AI-run companies could operate in just about any industry except banking. “An AIC may have any lawful purpose, regardless of whether for profit, except for the business of banking,” according to a draft bill that may be submitted to the Delaware state legislature.
The draft bill says AI agents could be “designated to manage the business and affairs, and to conduct the business, of the AIC.” The bill proposes a “regulatory sandbox” that would exist for 30 months to test the idea. Allowing AI-run companies would bring more revenue via taxes and fees to Delaware, which is already a top destination for business entities of all sizes.
In July 2026, Delaware’s Secretary of State Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez co-wrote an op-ed in Fortune announcing the proposal. The op-ed said that “nothing in the law of several states clearly prevents an AI agent from operating a company with no human at the helm,” and that states should develop legal frameworks for autonomous software that is able to contract, pay suppliers, and make transactions with no human involvement.
“The answer is not to try to prohibit the activity; any effort to do so is just as unlikely to succeed as the technology and its enablers are likely to push the boundaries of the law,” the op-ed said. “The answer is to wrap AI in legal form. Give an autonomous system a recognizable legal identity and you make it legible to law. You create a deﬁned target to which responsibility and damages can attach. You make the agent’s conduct visible, traceable, and accountable.”
The op-ed explained how an AI-run company will shield humans from legal liabilities:
A Delaware AIC will be a separate legal entity whose day-to-day aﬀairs are managed by an AI agent rather than a person. At the agent’s direction, the AIC can sue and be sued in its own name, hold and dispose of property, and incur obligations. It has a single member, a person or an entity, responsible for keeping the AIC adequately capitalized, and the AIC must keep a log of its activities. That member is shielded from the AIC’s debts, except where it fails to capitalize the company or uses it to commit fraud or a willful violation of law.
Under the proposed law, the “member” is an individual or a corporation that would fund the AI-run company and benefit from any profits, but designate an AI agent to manage the actual business. The draft bill says, “The member is not liable for any act or omission that the AIC takes or fails to take, or that another person takes or fails to take at the direction of the AIC.” There are exceptions for when a person uses the AI-run company “to engage in fraud or any willful violation of law,” or “caused or allowed the AIC to conduct business when the member knew or should have known the conduct was outside the AIC’s statement of purpose.”
Citing Patibanda-Sanchez’s announcement, Comer wrote that an AI-run company would provide “the human or entity capitalizing the AIC with liability protections from potential harms to business partners, consumers, and the public, perpetrated by the controlling AI.”
A spokesperson for Gov. Meyer told Ars today that “we have received the letter and are in the process of reviewing it.” A spokesperson for Patibanda-Sanchez declined to comment, saying that the governor’s office is handling press requests on the matter.
Patibanda-Sanchez’s op-ed said Delaware’s planned regulatory sandbox will “pilot agentic commerce in daylight, under supervision, with capital tied to liability and the ability to shut a system down.” The 30-month testing period would give the state legislature “a full record for deciding how to legislate” AI-run companies, it said.
A future state law allowing AI-operated companies would be especially impactful in Delaware, as about two-thirds of Fortune 500 companies are incorporated in the state. Although Elon Musk now prefers Texas , many corporations choose Delaware for its low corporate taxes and business-friendly legal framework. Patibanda-Sanchez boasts that Delaware provides “the most predictable and business-focused legal home in the world,” and that 334,461 new entities were formed in Delaware in 2025.
Patibanda-Sanchez collaborated on the sandbox plan with a private company that says it makes legal AI agents for businesses. “The framework for industry engagement with AICs is being developed in Delaware as part of a public-private partnership led by Norm Ai,” said the op-ed co-written by Patibanda-Sanchez and Norm Ai founder and CEO John Nay.
Meyer, a Democrat, publicly supported the idea of letting AI agents incorporate in a response to an April 2026 social media post by Mark Cuban. Cuban wrote , “If I was the governor of a state looking to grow their revenues, I would add the ability for anyone to incorporate using an AI agent and stablecoins. And charge a premium for the service. Post the agent in the marketplace/connectors that the big LLMs have, to simplify it for everyone. First to market makes a killing.”
Meyer’s official X account replied , “On it!” and posted a link to Meyer’s July 2025 announcement of the plan for an AI sandbox in which “artificial intelligence technologies can be safely developed and deployed across high-impact sectors, including corporate governance, biotechnology, healthcare, chemicals, and financial services.”
In July 2025, Meyer signed a legislative resolution “to create a regulatory sandbox framework for the testing of innovative and novel technologies that utilize agentic artificial intelligence.” This resulted in the Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission forming a Sandbox Subcommittee to work on a “draft regulatory framework that would create a regulatory sandbox that would test and evaluate agentic artificial intelligence and its application to corporate governance,” the commission said in its December 2025 annual report .
The commission said the Sandbox Subcommittee was working on “potential draft legislation,” and had received a briefing from Patibanda-Sanchez “on the work of a group she has formed to investigate a potential structure for a regulatory sandbox.”
In June 2026, the draft legislation was detailed in a Spotlight Delaware article that said the bill is likely to be introduced in the state legislature next year. The article said:
The principal drafter of the proposed legislation, John Mark Zeberkiewicz, said the measure could allow AI agents to engage in just about any business activity—from providing coding services to signing contracts, or even filing and defending lawsuits.
He also noted that it seeks to protect owners of new Artificial Intelligence Companies from faci

articles.title_orig: Canada, UAE sign trade deal as Carney seeks new trading partners
articles.title_zh: Canada, UAE sign trade deal as Carney seeks new trading partners
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Mark Carney hosts Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi at a state dinner in Ottawa on Monday. Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press
Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is courting wealthy Gulf investors, hosted a dinner in Ottawa on Monday for Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan of Abu Dhabi, the oil-rich heart of the United Arab Emirates.
A guest list of nearly 120 names obtained by The Globe and Mail shows many in Canada’s corporate elite were invited to dine with Sheikh Khaled and senior members of Abu Dhabi’s ruling circle.
The dinner capped the first day of a two-day visit to Canada by the Crown Prince, whose father is the president of the UAE.
Canada and UAE sign free trade deal, signal investment deals in energy sector ‘very soon’
The blossoming relationship between Canada and the UAE has included the inking of a free trade agreement in July and an investment protection treaty that went into force in May. Mr. Carney came back from a visit to the country last fall touting a UAE commitment to invest $70-billion in Canada.
Ottawa is deepening ties with the UAE and other foreign trade partners as part of a push by the Prime Minister to lessen Canada’s economic reliance on the United States.
One of the most prominent invitees to the dinner was former prime minister Stephen Harper. The list leaned toward companies and investors with stakes in defence and security, energy, critical minerals, infrastructure, international development, space, advanced communications, quantum computing and artificial intelligence – all areas in which the Prime Minister’s Office has said the two countries will expand relations.
Senior Carney aide Angad Singh Dhillon appointed Canada’s next UAE ambassador
The invitees also included lawyers, consultants and lobbyists representing business interests in Ottawa, as well as provincial representatives, hospital and university leaders, museum administrators and representatives of Indigenous communities.
Members of the Desmarais family, long synonymous with Power Corporation of Canada, were on the list. André Desmarais, deputy chairman of Power Corporation of Canada, and Paul Desmarais III, a senior vice-president, were both listed, along with executives from Power Sustainable, a Power Corp. investment arm.
Also among the invitees were representatives of several large industrial companies, including Gregory Ebel, chief executive of Enbridge Inc.; Ian Edwards of engineering firm AtkinsRéalis; Alexandre L’Heureux of WSP Global; Kieran Hawe of construction company EllisDon; Bruce Power’s chief operating officer, James Scongack; and Eric Desaulniers, head of graphite developer Nouveau Monde Graphite.
Victor Dodig, recently appointed chief executive of Telus Corp., was also listed, as was Éric Martel, chief executive of Bombardier Inc.
Members of the tech industry were invited, including Joelle Pineau, chief AI officer at Cohere, and Valérie Pisano, chief executive of Mila.
Big investors and lenders were also on the list, including Deborah Orida, chief executive of PSP Investments; Alison Nankivell of Export Development Canada; and Geneviève Bouthillier, an executive vice-president at BDC Capital. So were government-relations heads from Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, HOOPP and Sun Life, and venture investor Chris Arsenault of Inovia. Gurinder Grewal, named chief executive of Invest in Canada on Aug. 31, was also on the list.
Many members of Mr. Carney’s inner circle were listed, including Marc-André Blanchard, his chief of staff; Michael Sabia, Clerk of the Privy Council; David Morrison, a senior diplomatic adviser; Scott Gilmore, principal secretary; and Jennifer MacIntyre, a deputy chief of staff. The ambassadors to the United States and the UAE, Mark Wiseman and Angad Dhillon, were also on the list. So was Sébastien Carrière, Global Affairs Canada’s chief of protocol.
Many of the Emiratis who were invited work for the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince’s Court. Sheikh Khalifa bin Tahnoon Al Nahyan, the court’s chairman, and Saif Ghobash, chairman of the Crown Prince’s Office and secretary-general of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council, were listed, as was Sultan Al Jaber, who is both the UAE’s minister of industry and advanced technology and chief executive of the Abu Dhabi National Oil Co.
Among the rest of the Emirati contingent on the list were representatives of DP World, a Dubai-based port operator that on Monday announced a memorandum of understanding with the owner of Manitoba’s Port of Churchill to explore further development of an expanded northern shipping corridor. Douglas Smith, chief executive officer of the company’s operations in Canada, was invited, as was Sultan bin Saeed Al Mansoori, chairman of Dubai Chambers, who also sits on DP World’s board.
