articles.title_orig: AI debt fears ease ahead of Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon updates. Here's what to watch.
articles.title_zh: AI debt fears ease ahead of Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon updates. Here's what to watch.
articles.content_orig:
Fears over artificial intelligence debt have eased after a bout of volatility. But more tests for AI debt are coming.
Oracle holds its Investor Day on Wednesday. And hyperscalers Alphabet and Amazon.com are scheduled to report quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.
Credit markets are on edge over a flood of AI debt, though fears have eased up a little lately. Meta Platforms ' plans for a $95 billion stock offering , announced on Monday, helped bring down its credit-default swap spreads. Those spreads had risen last week when the company reported negative free cash flow in the third quarter. Other CDS spreads had moved higher too, though they have since backed off.
Investors had expected Meta to bring a large bond deal to market shortly after its earnings announcement, said Richard Cheng, head of Nuveen's investment-grade corporate sector team. The fact that it wasn't announced came as a relief.
"Just the absence of the bond deal itself is a direct catalyst for AI-related spread tightening," he said.
A credit spread is the difference in the yield between the corporate bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. When spreads tighten, it means investors are becoming more confident about the bond issuer.
The market action over the last few days shows that investors are recognizing that "credit fears may have been overblown," said CNBC contributor Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.
"I expect that these better feelings, maybe not good but better, may continue as companies announce their quarters over the next few weeks."
Still, spreads on CDS remain wider over the past year due to a surge of debt issuance and free cash flows turning negative across the AI space. Meta's CDS spread, for instance, is still up 177% year to date, while Amazon's spread has gained 129%.
Bond yields also remain elevated.
"It's not necessarily fundamentals," said CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin. "It's more, I'd say, 80% driven by technicals and sentiment."
Alphabet and Amazon pose the next big hurdle for tech bonds as they update their capex plans and free cash flow forecasts. Microsoft 's earnings are also due Wednesday, but the company has yet to issue any bonds to pay for its AI spending.
Both Amazon and Alphabet reported negative free cash flow in the second quarter and analysts expect that trend to continue.
Analysts expect Alphabet to report free cash flow of -$2.3 billion while spending $55.2 billion on capital expenditures in the third quarter, according to FactSet consensus estimates. Amazon is expected to report -$9.9 billion in free cash flow against capex of $58.7 billion.
S&P Global Ratings estimated in an August report that the hyperscalers will have negative free operating cash flow in 2026 and 2027.
More critical will be their outlooks, Cheng says. "The singular focus on the investors' minds is really what the capex guidance trajectory looks like across the hyperscaler space."
Meeks believes elevated capex is a sign of strong AI demand. The hyperscalers have "decided that with all the evidence they have — and they have more than you and me — that this is worthwhile spending, and not just worthwhile; it's required," he said.
CreditSights' Chalfin doesn't expect the hyperscalers to announce major new bond issuance around their earnings reports. Oracle's updates may be more critical for credit markets. The company has issued $117 billion in long-term debt and is clinging to an investment-grade credit rating of BBB-, the lowest level of investment grade above junk, according to S&P.
"It's the most important IG tech credit, just given how it's a bit more stressed relative to the A-rated names," he said. "It's trading more like a high-yield credit, even though it's IG, and so there's just a lot of investor concern on that one."
One wrinkle to the AI debt story: balance sheets don't reveal the whole picture. The companies are using complicated off-balance sheet arrangements for data centers and chip financing, and they aren't fully transparent, S&P Global said in a September report.
"There are commitments they are entering into, for example, into data center leases or purchase commitments on chips that aren't necessarily treated as debt," Mark Habib, digital infrastructure sector lead at S&P Global Ratings, said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Monday.
S&P is trying to provide the market with more visibility on those commitments "to give a fuller picture of what kinds of obligations they're actually entering into," he added.
Oracle aside, hyperscaler credit ratings are all comfortably above A levels — reflecting the fact that they have broadly diversified revenue streams, ample coverage for interest payments, and capacity to add leverage if they choose.
Nuveen's Cheng isn't concerned, pointing out that while there has been some credit repricing, there is no credit crisis.
"They continue to have exceptional credit profiles, strong cash generation liquidity," he said of the largest hyperscalers.
"The market is really not concerned about credit quality at this point," Cheng added. "It's really just the trajectory of the capex needs and the supply of debt to fund that. Both of those are pointing in one direction — and that's up."
Correction: This story has been revised to reflect that Oracle's investment-grade credit rating is BBB-, according to S&P. A previous version mischaracterized the company's credit rating.

articles.title_orig: Quebec’s separatist leader threatens to play spoiler at Carney’s EU summit
articles.title_zh: Quebec’s separatist leader threatens to play spoiler at Carney’s EU summit
articles.content_orig:
Quebec’s new separatist government accused Ottawa on Tuesday of barring the province from this week’s EU-Canada summit in Montreal and warned it would have the last word on any deals struck there that concern its powers.
The dispute erupted Tuesday morning when Quebec Justice Minister Marie-Claude Sarrazin said in a statement that Ottawa had refused Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon's request to address the summit, which opens Thursday.
St-Pierre Plamondon said in a post on X that the decision revealed a “serious lack of respect,” adding that Ottawa would rather he “serve shrimp cocktail” at a function rather than address one.
Ottawa also turned down a September request from the previous Quebec government to host a reception on the sidelines of the summit, Sarrazin noted.
Prime Minister Mark Carney hit back, saying St-Pierre Plamondon had himself turned down an invitation to the Thursday night summit dinner. “It’s his decision to leave an empty chair again,” Carney told reporters in French.
The tiff threatens to overshadow an international gathering that Carney, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa have billed as a step change in mutual relations, driven by U.S. President Donald Trump’s aggressive tariffs and scorn for the postwar Western consensus.
Early drafts of the joint declaration include a digital trade deal and a pact that lets the European Investment Bank finance Canadian critical minerals projects. Many of those deliverables fall under provincial jurisdiction, such as natural resources.
“'When you’re not at the table, you’re on the menu,' Prime Minister Carney told us,” Sarrazin said in her statement. “The federal government has chosen to prevent Quebec from having a say on its own territory.”
Whatever agreements are signed at the summit, “Quebec is sovereign in its fields of jurisdiction internationally, so it will have the last word,” Sarrazin warned.
Her statement evoked the 1965 Gérin-Lajoie doctrine, a principle of Quebec’s international policy that holds it can conduct its own foreign relations in areas the Canadian Constitution assigns to the provinces. It also noted that Quebec had a seat at the table during negotiations on CETA, the EU-Canada trade deal signed in 2015, attending more than 100 meetings.
Yves-François Blanchet, leader of the separatist Bloc Québécois in the federal parliament, also said he had been refused a request to attend. “You’re invited to come, but above all, keep quiet. Don’t speak,” he told reporters on Parliament Hill.
On Tuesday midmorning Ottawa time, Trump congratulated St-Pierre Plamondon on his election victory — three weeks after the actual Oct. 5 ballot — sharing an article headlined “Separatists win Quebec provincial election in blow to Mark Carney.”
Trump and Carney have been at odds since the dramatic implosion of mutual trade talks in late August, with the U.S. president deploring the Canadian leader as “nasty.”
The Quebec premier, meanwhile, is all-in on sovereignty in a province where support for separating from Canada reached a three-decade low of 29% earlier this year.
Carney rejected St-Pierre Plamondon’s claims of exclusion, saying Quebec had been consulted on the summit. “We have had three consultations with the Quebec delegation already on the agreement with the European Union,” he said. Carney’s office told POLITICO on Tuesday that it had invited every premier to attend the Thursday dinner in Montreal.
St-Pierre Plamondon also skipped a federal meeting with Indigenous leaders and premiers on Monday, an absence Carney criticized.
Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said the premier was “welcome” in Montreal, but that the summit was a federal meeting, with geopolitics a federal area of responsibility. “With everything going on in the world, we just need to make sure we can reach an agreement with the European Union,” she said. “That’s what Quebecers want.”
Despite the public spat over the summit logistics, working-level officials described the relationship between the different levels of government as constructive.
Hélène Drainville, Quebec’s delegate general in Brussels, told POLITICO on Monday that federal and provincial officials have set up joint working groups to implement the summit’s outcomes.
Quebec is also in talks with the European Investment Bank and DG GROW, the Commission’s industry department, about the bank’s entry into Canada, she said.
“Right now, all the signals are green,” Drainville said. She underlined, however, that the province “has to be at the table” if Ottawa and Brussels strike deals in its areas of jurisdiction.
Mickey Djuric and Sue Allan contributed reporting from Ottawa.

articles.title_zh: Free Elder Stuff in The Sims 4 October 2026 Patch
articles.content_orig:
Another month, another major update for The Sims 4! This time we're looking towards the Sims 4 October Patch, expected to arrive in less than one week, on October 27th, 2026 . This patch covers more content from August's Free Content Teaser, as well as tweaks and bug fixes that address autonomy issues, some forms of save corruption, and more. Read on for more info so you know what to expect!
The Sims 4 October Patch is going to be a bit of a doozy, adding long-requested changes and finally fixing issues players have been running into for months, or even years . On the brighter and less-concerning side of things, this patch will also add more content from the free content teaser shown in August of this year!
What items are being added were not specified during the Q&A or in the Laundry List, but we can get an idea based on August's Free Content teaser that showcased new CAS and Build Mode assets. These can be compared to the last two updates and their included assets to see what we could be expecting.
For the entire Q&A, including other discussed questions and answers not exactly relating to the Sims 4 October Patch, click below to read our recap!
Like other patches from 2026, The Sims 4 October Patch is going to be heavily focused on altering features, fixing long-standing bugs, and adding new items. This does not inherently mean that tons of mods will be broken with this update, just that there is a high chance of certain mods being broken or requiring updates for compatibility.
Since we won't know for sure until the patch actually drops, preparation is the most important thing for anybody who plays with mods and wants to protect their existing save files. If you play with mods, especially script mods and mods that add significant gameplay, saving over your save file without your script mods when they are automatically disabled due to a patch can cause unexpected, unintended, and possibly game-breaking problems.
Enabling mods without properly updating them can also cause issues, depending on the exact mod and what the update changes, adds, or removes.
With all that being said, we've made a general guide for these large updates to help you keep your beloved save files safe, so read on for help and tips to a happy & healthy Sims 4 game!
Especially if you are a Mods & Custom Content user and/or you play long-term save files like legacies, challenges, forever saves, etc., an important part of save file health and keeping them safe and playable is to back them up prior to updates.
This is primarily important for those who play with mods and custom content, as mods being disabled after previously being active in a save or mods being broken while active in a save can cause corruption and other issues.
Although creating back ups of files can sound a bit daunting if you're unfamiliar with the concept, it is fairly easy and painless.
Here are the steps for backing up saves:
Another good rule of thumb is that, if playing with mods or custom content, do not attempt to play save files you care about until creators have posted about the update and the status of their mods. Most major creators post fairly quickly, but be patient!
The Sims Team confirmed in a message on The Sims Discord that this Sims 4 Update will have an impact on mods:
This update is expected to have an impact on mods and we recommend you back up your saves and manage your mods/CC carefully.
Like most other updates, mods have a chance of breaking, especially if they change a feature that has been adjusted in the update. Custom content is often completely fine, but files can always corrupt or go wrong in some way. This means that, while it may seem tedious, the 50/50 method is the best way to find any issues that have popped up in your game that are stemming from broken or corrupted mods and custom content.
The 50/50 method is a way of organizing and testing mods and custom content to track down a specific file or files that are causing a bug or error in your game, or are causing it to not load or crash. Make sure to back up your saves, mods, and tray folders prior to this!
For a more in-depth guide to the 50/50 method, ThatSimsLady has broken it down previously and provided a guide that walks you through it , but here’s a general diagram from Sims After Dark.
Basically, the 50/50 method is when you split your mods folder down the middle, testing each half (Say, Half A and Half B) individually to rule out issues. For example, if the error or bug in questions persists in Half A but not Half B , then you know that the issue is held in Half A . You can safely sort away Half B and then split Half A and test either half, and so on and so forth.
This should help you track down problematic files fairly easily. And I will say that nobody likes doing the 50/50 method since it can take a long time, especially if you play with loads of mods and custom content, but is a very good way to make sure your game is in healthy condition and none of your saves are at risk.
In most cases, mods that break during updates are UI Mods and Gameplay Mods .
Gameplay Mods generally add or change features in The Sims 4, and many contain two files; .package and .ts4script files. While not always, these mods are prone to breaking with updates and should be removed and separately tested, or only updated/added back in once the creator has said it is safe.
UI Mods are any mods that change the user interface, like the menus surrounding your screen in Live mode and Build mode, or your columns in Create-A-Sim. The most commonly used UI mods include UI Cheats , More Columns in CAS , and any User Interface Replacement mods. While it is not inherent that they will break, they are usually the first to break during any update.
Also, always delete your thumbcache file. It regenerates every time the game launches, and should always be deleted while changing your mods folder in any way, especially if you're doing the 50/50 method.
It is also recommended to test mods with new updates in a completely fresh save file, to avoid corruption but also since certain updates only work with newer saves.
The biggest point is that your organization method makes sense to you , and you alone! As long as you can find where you put things and troubleshoot your

articles.title_orig: Report: iPhone 18 Pro sales down 4% in the US, but China drives 3.1% global growth
articles.title_zh: Report: iPhone 18 Pro sales down 4% in the US, but China drives 3.1% global growth
articles.content_orig:
Counterpoint Research’s latest report offers a look at global iPhone 18 Pro sales during the first three weeks of availability. Here are the details.
In a report released today, Counterpoint Research says iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max sales in the US fell 4% during their first three weeks of availability compared to the first three weeks of iPhone 17 Pro series sales last year.
The report noted that Japan saw a whopping 27% drop in sales, with demand weakening “as exchange rates amplified the price increases.”
China, on the other hand, saw a 29% increase in sales, while other markets collectively recorded a more modest 3.1% increase.
The report doesn’t break down what that means in units, or millions of units, but it does offer some context on what drove these regional differences.
A regional breakdown shows that the global 3.1% growth was concentrated in specific markets. China posted the strongest growth, with sales rising 29% YoY. This was driven by better early supply compared with last year and by price increases on competing flagship models from Chinese Android OEMs. Excluding China’s contribution, the global sales growth rate would have been far weaker. The US and Japan experienced a YoY decline, affected by higher prices compared with their predecessors. In the US, consumers largely do not perceive meaningful improvements over the previous models in either features or design, while in Japan, demand has contracted as exchange rates amplified the price increases.
Today’s report also includes another interesting tidbit: According to Counterpoint, the iPhone 18 Pro Max accounted for a slightly smaller share of Pro-series sales compared to last year’s iPhone 17 Pro series, which the firm attributed to higher prices and stronger demand for the smaller Pro model in emerging markets:
The iPhone 18 Pro Max accounted for 56% of sales within the iPhone 18 Pro series, a slight decrease from 57% last year. This can be attributed to the higher prices compared with last year, as well as the fact that the sales growth in emerging markets such as India and Southeast Asia skewed more toward the Pro models.
As to how, or whether, the iPhone Duo had any effect on these shifting numbers, the report didn’t address that directly, since the device launched after the three-week period covered by the data. However, Counterpoint Associate Director Sujeong Lim raised the possibility that it could affect Pro Max sales going forward:
“Whether China’s outperformance reflects durable demand or front-loaded buying will become clearer in the coming weeks. The recovery of US and Japanese volumes, and whether the iPhone Duo launching in Week 43 will generate incremental demand rather than cannibalising Pro Max, are the two most consequential near-term variables.”

articles.title_orig: Nvidia's worst nightmare may be lurking inside Anthropic's IPO filing
articles.title_zh: Nvidia's worst nightmare may be lurking inside Anthropic's IPO filing
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic is hedging its bets by using multiple chips to handle its AI work — a strategy that could eventually erode Nvidia's dominance.
The AI lab says it manages compute "as a single, fungible pool from multiple strategic partners" — with software that can direct its work to different chips depending on where they're most productive, according to Anthropic's S-1 filing , which came out Monday as the company prepares to go public.
Anthropic says it uses hardware from four chip families: Amazon Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and AMD GPUs.
That flexibility, which Anthropic said "took years and significant investment to build," could make major AI companies less dependent on Nvidia over time and give them more negotiating leverage, analysts said.
"The real exposure could be Nvidia's pricing power," said Patrick Moorhead, founder and CEO of Moor Insights & Strategy, "because a customer that can shift work across four platforms negotiates very differently than one that can't."
Ashish Nadkarni, an analyst at IDC, added that a multichip approach also makes Anthropic less vulnerable to fluctuations in Nvidia's chip supply.
Although Anthropic's chip mix isn't new, the company is now pitching it as a core advantage to investors, Moorhead said.
The threat has its limits. Switching between chips is still difficult — especially when it comes to training AI models as opposed to running them, Moorhead said — and only the biggest AI companies have the resources to do it.
Anthropic also continues to spend billions on Nvidia compute , Moorhead said.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said that while other major companies like OpenAI likely take a multichip approach, it may not be worth the effort and investment for smaller players.
Brad Gastwirth, global head of research and market intelligence at Circular Technology, said Anthropic's strategy doesn't represent a major near-term threat. Having more chip options doesn't erase Nvidia's advantages in performance, networking, and software, he said.
There's a broader risk for Nvidia if AI compute becomes more of a commodity.
Citadel CEO Ken Griffin has warned that if supply overtakes demand, it could drive down rental prices.
"GPUs, like airlines, have a very low marginal cost to run," he told Bloomberg last week. "The moment you have overcapacity, pricing goes into freefall."
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider.

articles.title_zh: ChatGPT’s Advice to Cut Her Seizure Drug Led to Devastating Consequences
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI is facing a lawsuit following allegations that its AI chatbot, ChatGPT, provided medical advice linked to a fatal epilepsy episode. The lawsuit, filed by the parents of Bowen Wan in San Francisco Superior Court, claims that ChatGPT diagnosed Wan and recommended a tapering off of her epilepsy medication, which allegedly resulted in her death. This case is part of broader litigation against OpenAI, which includes previous claims of dangerous medical guidance given by the chatbot. OpenAI has consistently maintained that ChatGPT is not a substitute for professional medical advice.
Markets will likely reflect any developments in the legal proceedings against OpenAI, as outcomes could significantly impact the company’s financial stability. Additionally, any statements from OpenAI regarding its financial health or strategic responses to these legal challenges could influence market expectations. Observers should also watch for any major funding activities or shifts in executive personnel at OpenAI, which could further affect bankruptcy predictions.

Pope Leo’s lung cancer diagnosis and surgery has affected how Catholics view his health and papacy, the Vatican’s foreign minister said on Tuesday, in an unusual acknowledgement by one of the Church’s most senior officials.

Leo, 71, had part of one lung removed in surgery on October 13. His doctors have said the cancer was localised and had not spread, and the pope will not require further treatment.

MINNEAPOLIS and RACINE, Wis. — Oct. 27, 2026 — You asked, Cheerios™ and Ziploc® Brand delivered – freshness you can reseal! After receiving hundreds of thousands of requests, comments and reactions annually on the topic, Cheerios and Ziploc® Brand have come together to introduce Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™. The new innovation features the first resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box, making it easier to pour, reseal and help keep cereal fresher longer.
The partnership brings together Cheerios, the No. 1 cereal brand*, with more than 50 years of Ziploc® Brand expertise helping people seal in freshness and store the foods they love. It’s a natural pairing for cereal lovers, 90% of whom say they already take extra steps beyond simply closing the cereal box to help preserve freshness*** like folding the bag, rolling it, clipping it or even transferring it to another container.
“General Mills has received letters, emails and DMs asking for an easier way to reseal a cereal box, and we decided it was time to partner with the ultimate freshness brand: Ziploc®,” said Emilie Knox, Vice President and Business Unit Director for Cheerios at General Mills. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they’ve been asking for, making the whole routine easier and more enjoyable.”
Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is made for how people want to pour a bowl of cereal, as well as store it. The resealable bag is designed to open only partially across the top to create a convenient “pour spout” as an easier way for the whole family to fill a bowl (or a cup, mug or even little hands). Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ then seals closed right inside the box for cereal freshness you can reseal.
“For generations, Ziploc® Brand has helped people keep the foods they love fresh through simple, trusted solutions,” said a Ziploc® Brand spokesperson. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is an exciting new expression of what Ziploc® Brand can do – bringing our resealable freshness expertise directly into the Cheerios package and Ziploc® Brand into the pantry in an entirely new way.”
Available as a new option in the cereal aisle for both Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios, Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ combines the same Cheerios families already reach for with Ziploc® Brand’s expertise in resealable storage, for an easier way to open, pour, reseal – and keep enjoying.
A fix that feels this intuitive was anything but simple. With nearly one box of Cheerios produced every second, the new Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ had to be developed to work at Cheerios scale while keeping the same familiar cereal flowing to pantries nationwide. For Ziploc® Brand, the partnership builds on a history of resealable storage that began with the introduction of its innovative zipper technology in 1968.
And there’s a fitting full-circle connection: Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is being produced exclusively in Buffalo, New York, in the same place where Cheerios was first made in 1941.
Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is now available exclusively at Walmart.com and will roll out to retailers nationwide in the coming months.

articles.title_orig: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
articles.title_zh: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
articles.content_orig:
Google has opened applications for the Android Registered App Stores program for third-party app stores outside the United States. The program will begin operating on December 1, 2026, and is intended to provide approved platforms with a simplified way to install apps on compatible Android devices, Ars Technica reports .
Users of approved stores will be able to install apps with one tap, similarly to Google Play. Such stores will also be able to update apps in the background without additional user actions.
Google said the program is intended to give third-party stores a more convenient route to users while maintaining the security requirements of the Android ecosystem. This mechanism will not operate in the United States: there, under the court ruling in the Epic Games case, alternative stores can be distributed through Google Play. Aptoide is currently among those represented in Google Play.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram .
Store operators must confirm the protection of intellectual property, the removal of illegal content, and the existence of a privacy policy for users and developers. They are also required to maintain ongoing security measures so as not to facilitate the distribution of malicious software. When applying, they must provide the relevant documentation in English and upload copies of all the store's apps.
Participation in the program will cost $10,000 per year, and the fee must be paid before the application is reviewed. Google explains that the funds will cover additional program support. The company may also charge an additional review fee if it identifies malware-related issues in a store.
Support is planned to be introduced in dozens of countries, mainly outside the United States and Europe. At the same time, the program will work only on devices with current Android 17 versions: support will begin with Android 17 QPR2, which is expected to arrive on Pixel smartphones in the coming weeks.

World of Warcraft 's new housing system has provided a segment of the player base with things to do, collect, and create beyong the typical raiding gameplay loop, but already it is becoming egregious for its monetization layers.
World of Warcraft 's Housing gameplay feature has acquired some decor items for sale for real money, which isn't a first.
The new bundles are called the Haunted Grimtide Estate for $25 on Battle.net and the Grimtide Decor Pack for $10 on Battle.net . However, selling items tied to a playable race in theme is indeed a first.
The items within these bundles are spooky furniture and decorations themed after the Kul Tiran player race, as these items have a pirate and Lovecraftian aesthetic. However, players are not happy about this arrangement, owing to Blizzard's previous promises about its microtransaction practices for housing.
@Wowhead Kul Tiran housing decor in the shop directly contradicts Blizzard's housing principles from less than a year ago.
It was literally principle #2. https://t.co/UOkELnupW3 October 27, 2026
X users and even famed content creators like @BellularGaming responded to this , pointing out that Blizzard Entertainment is contradicting itself, reminding us that the company swore never to sell housing decor tied to player races for real money.
The promise in question came from a developer blog post Blizzard made on November 6, 2025 , where it said, and I quote, " Housing items tied to core fantasies of a player’s race or class, or that already exist in Azeroth, won’t be sold in the shop . Thematically important decor that players know and love will also not appear in the shop."
We've reached out to Blizzard for further comment regarding this situation.
Housing was one of the most requested gameplay features ever since the 2000s, as players wanted a place for their characters and guilds to call home.
Unfortunately, while the actual gameplay of Housing was good, it was marred by controversial housing cosmetic DLC items that cost just as much as an expansion . Add this betrayal of trust on Blizzard's part, and much of the hype and goodwill surrounding this long-awaited feature has been sucked away, much like the rest of this expansion.
So far, the vast majority of playable races in WoW don't have exterior decor options, some don't even have interior decor options in abundance. Getting items can be an absolutely monstrous grind, and unlike other similar games with housing systems like Fallout 76 , you need to buy each individual piece, limiting creativity.
Personally speaking, World of Warcraft: Midnight has been a non-stop disappointment with its weak storyline , dishonor to the Horde , constant bugs , and rushed content , and this just adds more salt to the wound.
Here's hoping the prices drop on these cosmetics at least, and that the next expansion, World of Warcraft: The Last Titan, as well as World of Warcraft: Forever , turn out to be much better experiences.

articles.title_orig: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
articles.title_zh: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
articles.content_orig:
United Parcel Service on Tuesday reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The guidance raise comes after the company already upped its outlook last quarter . UPS now said it's projecting full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion.
Shares of UPS rose slightly in morning trading.
Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Sept. 30, UPS reported net income of $1.16 billion, or $1.37 per share, down slightly from net income of $1.31 billion, or $1.55, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time expenses, UPS reported earnings per share of $1.69. Revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion.
In its domestic segment, the company said it saw a 4.5% increase in revenue, while its international segment had a 7.1% rise in revenue. Its supply chain solutions business saw an 18.2% revenue increase, which UPS said was primarily driven to growth in forwarding and logistics, including healthcare . On a call with analysts, CEO Carol Tomé said healthcare revenue exceeded $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter.
The company had previously said it expected its third-quarter domestic revenue to be flat and for domestic average daily volume to fall due to seasonal declines and the glide down with Amazon .
"We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network," Tomé said on the call. "All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."
UPS has been in the midst of a turnaround under Tomé's leadership, working to create a leaner business model and leveraging automation to position the company for growth.
As the company prepares for its peak holiday season, Tomé said the consumer remains resilient, and the growth in average daily volume between the third and fourth quarters will be consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume is expected to fall due to the reduction with Amazon.
She added that nearly 70% of all packages will flow through an automated process this holiday season.

articles.title_orig: Why Anthropic's IPO contrasts the 'cult of Elon Musk' at SpaceX and Tesla
articles.title_zh: Why Anthropic's IPO contrasts the 'cult of Elon Musk' at SpaceX and Tesla
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
In the first mega IPO of 2026, SpaceX ( SPCX ) singled out one person in its prospectus as the shot caller: none other than the world's richest person, Elon Musk.
The next big IPO of the year — Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), which could be the largest of all time — is run more by a committee of founders. That's a good thing given its mission and structures, according to veteran dealmaker Jim Neeson.
"I would say having seven founders working together can make it where it's not just like a cult of Elon Musk, right?" the Connor Group founding executive said on Sozzi Unleashed . "You actually have it where you have a consortium of people making decisions, which I actually think can be a good thing."
Neeson noted that Anthropic is a public benefit company with seven founders who collectively own 50.1%.
"You have a board that will be approved by sort of a trust fund. And then you also have a business where it's not just going to be about profits. It's also going to be sort of the social benefit piece that's built into their doctrine," he explained.
Anthropic's founders are CEO Dario Amodei and his sister and president, Daniela Amodei, as well as Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Chris Olah. The consortium left OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) to start Anthropic in January 2021.
The seven co-founders will be issued new Class F common stock as part of the IPO, giving them majority control of the company — something Neeson said investors will have to navigate.
"If you look at Meta, [and] you also look at Google, you had very strong founders," Neeson said. "A lot of times that is the venture capital case. I want founders that can make strong decisions and not be beholden to sort of quarterly type of trends."
"This is going to be a different type of structure out there, and it's going to be tested," he added. "We've never seen it, especially at this scale, especially at these growth rates. So I would say that's one thing analysts and investors are going to be looking very closely at."
The group looks to be managing the financials relatively well.
Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, the prospectus showed. The filing also discloses an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, a strong signal of aggressive AI spending in the years ahead.
On an adjusted basis, Anthropic posted $1.62 billion in operating income through the first six months of 2026 compared to a loss of $1.85 billion last year.
Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.
Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

Brent holds near $115 as Iran war tensions and escalating Saudi-Houthi hostilities keep oil markets on edge ahead of U.S. midterms.
Hormuz Becomes Even More Dangerous — and More Expensive
- October has seen the most acute escalation in maritime attacks since the US-Iran war started eight months ago, with already more than 30 incidents recorded in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways, up from 14 in September.
- The most recent addition to the list of maritime targets is a crude tanker in Iraq's exclusive economic zone, signaling that it is not only tankers seeking to surreptitiously transit the Hormuz that get targeted by Iran.
- VLCCs, the largest crude tankers available, account for 28% of all drone and missile attacks in the Persian Gulf, with the 32 impacted ships representing almost 4% of the global VLCC fleet.
- Freight rates from the Gulf remain elevated with a Saudi Arabia-China voyage still costing around $33 per barrel, whilst regional demurrage rates have been rising since mid-August to their current level of $1,000,000/day.
- UKMTO, a provider of maritime security alerts, recently admitted that it is becoming increasingly more difficult to report on strikes as transiting ships prefer to sail unnoticed and charterers are wary of pushing freight rates even higher.
- US gas producer EQT (NYSE:EQT) has agreed to buy Range Resources (NYSE:RRC) in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US gas company, with the combined Appalachian-focused company having a net output of more than 9 bcf/d.
- US energy firm Ovintiv (NYSE:OVV) will acquire Canada's Logan Energy in an all-cash deal valued at $0.9 billion, adding around 20,000 boe/d of production and 266,000 net acres across the Montney shale play.
- UK oil major BP (NYSE:BP) has started the second phase of exploration in Venezuela's offshore Loran gas field, using the research and survey vessel Fugro Brasilis to perform final seabed studies.
- US oil giant ExxonMobil (NYSE:XOM) reported a commercial discovery with its Rockhead-1 exploration well offshore Guyana, its first drilling success since the 2024 Hatchetfish find with a resource estimate of 500-600 million barrels.
- Italian oil major ENI (BIT:ENI) has launched the construction of its 3 TCf Cronos project offshore Cyprus, aiming for first gas in the first half of 2028, to be exported via Egypt's Damietta LNG terminal. Tuesday, October 27, 2026
The oil markets are counting down the days until the November 3 midterm elections in the US, with expectations of impending hostilities rising into next month. Last-minute efforts to negotiate some form of de-escalation are ongoing, with both Qatar and Pakistan seeking to mediate between the Trump administration and Tehran, temporarily capping the upside for ICE Brent at $115 per barrel. Simultaneously to Hormuz tensions, the Saudi-Houthi conflict appears to be gaining self-sustaining momentum.
OPEC+ Holds the Fort on Supply Hikes. OPEC+ is expected to hold December output targets steady at its Sunday's meeting, with seven core members focusing on 2027 production quotas instead after they've completed the roll-back of 1.65 million b/d voluntary cuts, disrupted by the Hormuz crisis.
US Moves China Shipping Fees into 2027. The US is considering extending its truce with China on port charges for Chinese-linked ships by two months to January 9, preserving a suspension of tit-for-tat fees that previously imposed millions of dollars per port call and raised freight costs.
Houthis Hit Saudi Arabia's Largest Refinery. Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike hit Saudi Arabia's 550,000 b/d Ras Tanura refinery, causing a fire and disrupting operations at the Middle Eastern kingdom's largest plant, with an earlier March attack shutting it for three months.
Refining Boom Derails Galp–Moeve Merger. Portugal's Galp and Spain's Moeve have abandoned plans for a potential downstream merger that would've combined 700,000 b/d of refining capacity and 3,500 service stations, claiming that 2026 bumper profits made it harder to agree M&A terms.
Brussels Builds a European Wall Against China. The European Union may introduce quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery from early 2027, seeking to replicate its recent import caps on hybrid vehicles as it struggles to narrow its €360 billion trade deficit.
Singapore Launches First LNG Term Tender. Singapore's state gas buyer GasCo launched its first ever LNG term supply tender after neighbouring Indonesia had announced it would slash pipeline gas exports by 15% to 31 MMCf/d , just as the government plans to add 5 new gas-powered plants.
East Timor Buys Out Its Untapped Offshore Gem. Australia's major Woodside (ASX:WDS) has agreed to sell its stakes in the Greater Sunrise fields offshore East Timor for $200 million to the island nation, leaving state oil firm Timor gap as the only stakeholder of the untapped 5.3 TCf field.
Alberta Pushes for Scrapping of Tanker Ban. The province of Alberta called on the Carney government to repeal Canada's 2019 West Coast tanker ban that bars vessels carrying over 12,500 tonnes from loading at British Columbia ports, backing a proposed 250,000 b/d crude-by-rail route.
Indonesia Gives Up on Market-Based Imports. Indonesia plans to replace tender-based crude oil and refined product imports with government-to-government (G2G) and government-to-business (G2B) agreements to secure supplies, courting India and China for long-term supply deals.
Dangote Considers Third African Refinery. Nigeria's Dangote conglomerate is considering building a third 700,000 b/d refinery in Africa, alongside the existing plant in Lekki and the upcoming Kenyan refinery in Lamu, whilst simultaneously investing into refined product pipelines in West Africa.
Malaysia Doubles Down on Coal. The Malaysia government has proposed extending the lifespan of its existing coal-fuelled power plants despite an earlier pledge to retire coal by 2044, with coal accounting for 56% of current generation as JKM prices jumped to $33 per MMBtu this week.
Iron Ore Plunges Again on China Demand Fears. Iron ore prices fell to their lowest since September 2024 as weak Chinese demand and wafer-thin margins are expected to curb Q4 steel consumption, sending the Dalian iron ore futures to ¥662 per tonne, below the $100 per tonne threshold. White House to Ease Methane Emission Rules. The Trump administration is planning to relax rules on methane emissions from oil and gas operations, including exemptions for wells producing up to 15 boe/d, projecting incremental output of 210 million barrels for older and depleted wells.
Bahri Orders Three New VLCCs to Expand Tanker Fleet. Saudi national shipping company Bahri has ordered three VLCCs from domestic shipbuilder International Maritime Industries for $451 million, with deliveries scheduled in 2029-30 and marking the first attempt at exclusively Saudi shipbuilding.
UK Considers Fast-Track Approvals for Tiebacks. The UK's Burnham government is considering the fast-tracking of a small number of oil and gas tiebacks before pending legislation creates Transitional Energy Certificates that extend existing fields but preserve the country's exploration ban.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has commented on Operation Veles on the Kupiansk front, during which Ukraine's defence forces, under the command of the Khartiia Corps, advanced more than 15 km underground into the Russian rear.

Quote: " Our important operation in the Kupiansk sector. More than 100 Russian occupiers have already been eliminated, and more than 30 have been taken prisoner. The underground advance has exceeded 15 k m."
Details: Zelenskyy added that Russian forces had previously attempted to use underground gas pipelines to advance through Ukrainian positions and launch assaults.
Quote: " Ukrainian warriors have successfully transformed this tactic, moderni s ed it, and made it much more sophisticated and technologically advanced. We are protecting the lives of our people, inflicting losses on the occupiers, and achieving our objectives in the Kupiansk sector. "
Background: Earlier, the Khartiia Corps reported that during Operation Veles on the Kupiansk front, Ukrainian forces advanced more than 15 km through underground tunnels behind Russian lines and captured more than 30 Russian soldiers.

articles.title_orig: Google to report Q3 results as investors focus on AI growth, weigh Meta Muse AI risk
articles.title_zh: Google to report Q3 results as investors focus on AI growth, weigh Meta Muse AI risk
articles.content_orig:
Alphabet ( GOOGL +1.19% ) ( GOOG +0.84% ) has turned heads with one particular number in recent months: $514 billion. That's the size of the Google Cloud backlog, or the value of customer contracts Alphabet has signed but hasn't yet turned into revenue. This enormous number shows just how hungry businesses are for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power.
But when the tech powerhouse reports third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Oct. 28, I'd argue that other figures will matter more. Let's dive in for a close look.
Image source: Getty Images.
First, though, let's take a quick look at Alphabet's path so far. You probably use the company's key product daily as you surf the internet, and this is the Google platform . Advertisers, knowing how much time we spend here, flock to Alphabet, making advertising the company's biggest earnings engine. Search and other advertising brought in $63 billion in the second quarter, for a 17% increase.
But as the AI boom advanced, Google Cloud emerged as the star of the show. That unit's second-quarter revenue jumped 82% to $24 billion, while its operating income more than tripled to $8.8 billion. Cloud operating margin widened to more than 35% from about 20% a year earlier. Meanwhile, the backlog climbed about $50 billion from the prior quarter.
Though this is great, a backlog shouldn't be confused with actual revenue. Instead, it's more like a promise. Alphabet says it expects to recognize a little more than half of the $514 billion over the next 24 months, and the rest will come in later. The figure also includes sales of Alphabet's custom AI chips, or TPUs, to customers, with most of that revenue expected in 2027. Of course, investors would love to see a growing backlog on Oct. 28, but there are more important elements to watch.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/27/26
First, cloud margins. Alphabet is still supply-constrained, so in the third quarter it plans to use capacity from third parties while it continues its build-out. Management warned this would create slight margin pressure. In the upcoming report, investors hope to see that any decline from the current margin level will be small.
Second, spending and free cash flow. Capital expenditures reached nearly $45 billion in the latest quarter, and free cash flow was negative $5.9 billion. Alphabet raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to the range of $195 billion to $205 billion and said spending will keep marching higher next year. Though trailing 12-month operating cash flow of $185.7 billion helps, investors will be eager to see signs that capex is turning into revenue.
Third, Search. Search, representing a huge chunk of Alphabet's revenue, will be a point to watch. AI features have been driving more usage, and the continuation of this is key.
There's reason to be optimistic about Alphabet's upcoming report. In the last earnings call, Alphabet chief Sundar Pichai said Alphabet has "gotten more bullish on the opportunities ahead" over the past year. And peers have been equally positive, noting sustained AI demand.
Investors should also keep in mind that Alphabet's ad revenue generates the cash flow that helps fund the AI build-out, and the Google platform offers diversification if any AI headwinds arise.
So, how should you approach Oct. 28? A significant backlog number is easy to cheer, but it's only the starting point. If cloud margins hold up, spending shows a path to revenue, and Google Search keeps growing, the rest of this story should look bright. If margins slip or revenue disappoints, even a large backlog may not be enough to please investors.
That said, it's important to hold off on focusing uniquely on one quarter and instead, keep your eye on the long term. Alphabet is profitable, diversified, and investing aggressively to serve AI demand. And all of that makes this tech player a fantastic long-term stock to own , whether you buy before or after Oct. 28.

articles.title_orig: The Trump admin said energy costs were a small price to pay in Iran war, but U.S. consumers are paying nearly 8x more than anyone else in fuel costs
articles.title_zh: The Trump admin said energy costs were a small price to pay in Iran war, but U.S. consumers are paying nearly 8x more than anyone else in fuel costs
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
WASHINGTON — Late September in the Oval Office, President Trump declared, “Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. We’re gonna win that war very soon.”
It wasn’t the first time he’s described the hostilities as “war.”
On Feb. 28, the day U.S. and Israeli began bombarding Iran, he warned that “the lives of courageous American heroes may be lost, and we may have casualties. That often happens in war, but we’re doing this not for now. We’re doing this for the future, and it is a noble mission.”
But throughout seven months of back-and-forth strikes with Iran, Trump administration officials, and sometimes Trump himself, have performed verbal acrobatics to avoid the “W” word.
Senior administration officials loosely tossed around “war” during the first stages of conflict, but with polls showing the war in unpopular and congressional support waning, “war” and even “Operation Epic Fury” have become taboo among members of the Trump administration.
Trump has called attacks on Iran a “military operation,” “military decimation,” “excursion” and “skirmish.”
At a White House press briefing last month, Vice President JD Vance attempted to clear the air when a reporter asked about a potential end to what she called a “war in Iran.”
“I wouldn’t call it a war right now,” Vance said. “Major combat operations lasted for about six weeks.”
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth tread carefully in front of the Senate Appropriations Committee in July, repeatedly referring to a “conflict” in Iran that needed additional funding to continue.
On May 5, during the first of two delicate ceasefires with Iran, Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced an end to the objectives laid out in Operation Epic Fury and the beginning of “Project Freedom” — an effort to escort merchant ships through the Strait of Hormuz.
In April, Trump announced the blockade of Iranian ports . When asked about whether the blockade constituted an act of war, Rubio replied, “That’s not an act of war, that’s a defensive measure. It’s a counter to what they have decided to do.”
Senior Trump officials have maintained that the conflict can no longer be viewed as war because the intensity of strikes between the two countries has been reduced.
The “end” of Operation Epic Fury, the name Trump used when he announced hostilities on Feb. 28, was declared on May 5 — 60 days after the fighting began.
The timing was no coincidence. Under the War Powers Resolution of 1973 , a president must cease all hostilities abroad after 60 days if there is no congressional declaration of war.
Under the Constitution, only Congress declares war, but past presidents have routinely circumvented this rule by exercising their authority to direct the military and initiate strikes on targeted nations.
Nearly every modern president, from Dwight D. Eisenhower to Trump, has used this justification to undertake military action without the declaratory approval of Congress.
Congress can also choose to approve an Authorization for Use of Military Force, which grants the president legal authority to conduct military operations overseas.
Unless Congress sets a time limit on the authorization, authority to use the legal justification to launch military strikes can theoretically span multiple administrations.
Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), a former constitutional law professor at American University, said that presidents of both parties have avoided the term “war” when attempting to evade congressional approval of hostile action abroad.
“Trump has followed some of his predecessors in playing word games with the war power,” Raskin said. “What makes his case so extreme is that he proudly described it as a war and depicted it in glorified military terms.”
In March, seven days into the fighting, Trump said, “The war itself is going unbelievably . It’s as good as it can be.”
Congress has not officially declared war since World War II. The Vietnam War, the invasion of Afghanistan and both wars in Iraq were all approved by Congress under the umbrella of an Authorization for the Use of Military Force.
This year Congress has not approved such an authorization for the action with Iran. Fourteen Senate votes for a War Powers Resolution to curb Trump’s war efforts have failed in the chamber so far.
According to a CNN/SSRS poll last month, only 26% of Americans approve of the Trump administration’s handling of the Iran war.
Raskin said that he believes Trump’s terminology has shifted with the public mood, adding that he hasn’t heard any of his Republican colleagues “play along with the semantic games.”
“When things have turned south in the fortunes of this war, he has tried to pretend it’s something else,” Raskin said. “I think that has just further enraged the population.”
The administration’s declaration that Operation Epic Fury had concluded echoed May 2003, when then-President George W. Bush stood in front of a banner reading “Mission Accomplished” aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln , approximately six weeks after Operation Iraqi Freedom began.
“Major combat operations in Iraq have ended,” Bush said. “And now our coalition is engaged in securing and reconstructing that country.”
Despite the victory lap, combat operations in Iraq and across the Middle East continued through the aughts. The Iraq war wouldn’t officially end until 2011, with President Obama’s signature.
Obama himself relied heavily on the 2001 Authorization for the Use of Military Force — passed by Congress under Bush — in his military campaign against  Islamic State during his presidency.
According to Council on Foreign Relations data , Obama launched 542 drone strikes and killed 3,797 people in Yemen, Pakistan and Somalia without renewed approval from Congress.
A case more analogous to Trump’s comes in former President Truman’s unilateral decision to deploy U.S. troops to Korea in 1950. The Truman administration forwent congressional approval altogether and used United Nations Security Council resolutions to justify the intervention against Communist forces in the north, according to a White House news release from the time.
There were many critics of this exercise of executive war powers, most notably, Ohio Republican Sen. Robert A. Taft, who argued that Truman had usurped congressional war powers.
However, that Congress still provided monetary support, granting Truman military funds and extensions to the draft to raise additional troops for the Korean War effort. According to historical Gallup polls , 78% of Americans in 1950 approved of U.S. intervention in Korea.
While Vance and other administration officials continue to avoid “war,” it does slip out now and then. Trump has been, perhaps, the most discordant messenger of the administration when discussing Iran.
After referring to the “war” on social media and public interviews more than a dozen times , Trump backed Vance’s comments about the Iran war no longer being active as he spoke to reporters in the Oval Office in September. He refuses to call the conflict a “war,” Trump said, because “you are supposed to get approval.”
“I call it a military conflict, because it’s small potatoes for us,” Trump said.

articles.title_orig: US’s RFK Jr claims Arabs ‘don’t produce science’: Why he’s very, very wrong
articles.title_zh: US’s RFK Jr claims Arabs ‘don’t produce science’: Why he’s very, very wrong
articles.content_orig:
United States Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has sparked uproar with comments he has made denying Arab contributions to mathematics, science and literature.
In a high-voltage rant on Monday, the US health secretary said, “There’s five hundred million Arabs in the world. And yet they don’t produce science. They don’t win the Nobel Prize. They don’t win the Fields Prize. They don’t win the Wolf Prize. They don’t produce literature.”
RFK Jr, who has been involved in anti-vaccine campaigns and has promoted a debunked theory linking vaccines to autism, made the comments during a US election campaign event in Grand Rapids, Michigan while supporting Republican nominee Mike Rogers, who is up against Arab-American Democrat nominee Abdul El-Sayed, in a tightly contested battle for Michigan’s Senate seat in next week’s midterm elections.
Critics said the comments were racist, Islamophobic and factually inaccurate, pointing to modern and historic Arab innovation in multiple fields.
Here’s how Arabs have made vital contributions to the human understanding of maths, science and literature through the centuries.
The period known as the Islamic Golden Age, from around 750 AD to 1258 AD, produced many key Arab contributions to medicine at a time when Europe was said to be in its Dark Ages. During this time, Arabic was the language of science and scholarship.
1st-4th centuries: The numerals 0-9, which originated in ancient India, were adopted by Arab mathematicians who spread them across the world. They displaced Roman numerals as a more advanced number system in mathematics.
8th century: Arab and Persian mathematicians were studying the ancient Indian concept of zero in mathematics in Baghdad, long before the Europeans. The number zero was crucial to the development of mathematics – but was absent from widely used Roman numerals in Europe.
813-833: The Arab mathematician Muḥammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi – one of those studying the number 0 – is often referred to as the “father of algebra” as he was the first to treat the method as a separate mathematical discipline in his work, Al-Jabr. This method provided the first linear and quadratic equations, still used as a core part of mathematical study today.
965-1040: Ibn al-Haytham, known as the “father of modern optics”, explained the role that light entering the eye plays in human vision. He was born in Basra in Iraq, but spent most of his working life in Cairo attending to noble families.
936-1013: Abu al-Qasim al-Zahrawi, called “the father of modern surgery”, was considered the greatest surgeon in the Middle Ages. He wrote a 30-volume encyclopaedia detailing medical practices and designed and illustrated many surgical instruments. Born in Azahara, in Andalusia, he was known as Abulcasis in Europe.
9th century: Fatima al-Fihri founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco. It is often cited as the oldest continually operating university.
1213-1288: Ibn al-Nafis described pulmonary circulation – the process by which blood passes through the lungs – several centuries before Europeans understood it. He wrote more than 110 volumes of work on surgery, ophthalmology and philosophy while working as a chief physician in Egypt.
915-965: Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi, regarded as the greatest poet in the Arabic language, was Yemeni and grew up immersed in Bedouin Arabic culture. He wrote in classical Arabic and many of his verses became sayings used in everyday Arabic.
1100-1165: Muhammad al-Idrisi was a geographer known for making the Tabula Rogeriana, one of the most accurate and detailed medieval world maps, and a high point of Islamic geography. He was born in Ceuta in Morocco.
In more modern times, RFK Jr’s assertion that Arabs do not win Nobel prizes for science and literature is very far from the truth. Here are some of the highlights:
Peter Medawar won the Nobel Prize for Medicine for work on for work on acquired immune tolerance, which underpins organ transplantation. He was born in Brazil to a Lebanese father.
Michael Atiyah won the Fields Medal, the most prestigious award for mathematics, in 1966. He was born in London to a Lebanese father and Scottish mother. Educated in Egypt, he spent much of his childhood in Cairo and Khartoum.
Egyptian Naguib Mahfouz won the Nobel Prize in Literature for his body of work, including the Cairo Trilogy, which the Swedish Academy said formed “an Arabic narrative art that applies to all mankind”. He is still the only winner of the prize who wrote in Arabic.
Elias James Corey won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for developing retrosynthetic analysis. He is an American of Lebanese descent.
Egyptian Ahmed Zewail won the Wolf Prize for Chemistry. The Wolf Prize is an international award which has been presented to living scientists and artists every year in Israel by the Wolf Foundation since 1978.
Zewail also won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for pioneering femtochemistry, which is the study of chemical reactions on extremely short timescales. He also won the Wolf Prize in Chemistry in 1993.
Egyptian scientist Mohamed ElBaradei shared his Nobel Prize with the International Atomic Energy Agency, which he led.
Omar M Yaghi,  born in Jordan to a Palestinian refugee family, won the Wolf Prize in Chemistry in 2018 for work on metal-organic frameworks. He shared the prize with Japan’s Makoto Fujita. The Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) condemned his acceptance of the award because the prize is awarded by an Israeli foundation.
Moungi Bawendi won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for the discovery and synthesis of quantum dots. He was born in France to a Tunisian father, but based in the US.
Yaghi also won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks. These are crystalline materials with large internal cavities that can capture and store gases, harvest water from air, and trap pollutants. He shared the prize with Susumu Kitagawa from Japan and Richard Robson from Australia.
In a post on X, vaccine scientist Peter Hotez of the Texas Medical Center weighed in on historical Arab scholarship, saying, “It was the Arab scientists of the Middle Ages who kept Aristotle, Hippocrates, Galen alive to hand it down in the Renaissance.”
Broadcaster Mehdi Hasan described RFK Jr’s comments as “racist” and, in a post on X, wrote: “One of the men who won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry last year was a Palestinian-American, Omar Yaghi.”
The Council on American-Islamic Relations called for the US health secretary to be removed. It said: “To stand on a public stage as a sitting US cabinet official and dehumanise half a billion people – and millions of Muslim and Christian Arab Americans – with fabricated, white supremacist talking points is utterly disqualifying for public office. His sweeping erasure of Arab contributions to humanity is not only maliciously false, but it also fans the flames of anti-Arab and anti-Muslim hate at a time when communities are already vulnerable to bigoted attacks from other public officials nationwide.”

Alaska Airlines will launch its first nonstop service between Anchorage (ANC) and Tokyo Narita (NRT)* next spring, creating a convenient new connection between Alaska and the Asia-Pacific region. The route will operate seasonally between Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport and Narita International Airport.
Operated on a Boeing 737 MAX 8 , the Anchorage-Tokyo Narita flight is designed to help guests feel comfortable, cared for and connected throughout the journey. In First Class, guests enjoy priority boarding, recliner seats, and elevated , multi-course d ining , starting with Alaska ’s Signature Charcuterie . F or a more rest ful experience, plush Filson-designed blankets, pillows and a Filson travel amenity kit featuring Salt & Stone products are provided. First Class guests also have access to the Alaska Lounge in Anchora g e wit h West Coast -inspired light meals, wines, brews and cocktails in a relaxing space . Main Cabin and Premium Class guests can settle in with a complimentary meal, including a hot entrée and dessert , with vegetarian options available . Additionally, Premium Class guest s can enjoy a curated selection of complimentary West Coast non-alcoholic and alcoholic beverages .
Atmos ™ Rewards members will enjoy free Wi-Fi thanks to T-Mobile on select flights as installation of ultra-fast Starlink Wi-Fi continues across Alaska’s MAX 8 narrowbody fleet.
Alaska Airlines has connected Alaskans to the people and places that matter since 1932, and we’re thrilled to connect Alaska and Japan. This long-requested route will open new opportunities for tourism and commerce, bringing our distinctive hospitality to more travelers and strengthen our growing global network.
Regional Vice President , Alaska Airlines
The people of the state of Alaska are ready to welcome leisure and business travelers to Anchorage on Alaska Airlines. As the only U.S. domestic carrier serving Tokyo with scheduled service, the opportuniti es to see the Northern Lights or visit Denali National Park are closer than ever . We also appreciate the many resource and business pa rtner ships in Japan and see those ties strengthening in the future with easy, nonstop flights.
Starting today through Oct. 31, round-trip introductory fares start at $999 for travel from Anchorage to Tokyo Narita from May 13 through June 7, 2027, subject to availability. Tickets are on sale now at alaskaair.com and hawaiianairlines.com. All new routes are subject to government approval. Terms and conditions apply; round-trip purchase required.
The Tokyo launch anchors another expansion of Alaska Airlines’ Anchorage network in 2027, including new seasonal nonstop service to Nashville (BNA), Austin (AUS), and Dallas-Ft. Worth (DFW). Together, the new routes will create the largest nonstop schedule from the state of Alaska in the airline’s history, expanding access to key destinations and reinforcing its commitment to the state as it celebrates 95 years of service next year.
Our ambitions are global, but our foundation remains the same. From the beginning, Alaska Airlines has connected communities across Alaska, the West Coast and beyond. From Anchorage to Tokyo and destinations around the globe, we’re building on that legacy and giving our guests more ways to explore the world with Alaska Airlines.
Regional Vice President , Alaska Airlines

articles.title_orig: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
articles.title_zh: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
articles.content_orig:
The BBC's Madina Maishanu shows the conditions inside the cell where so many died
An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls.
Forensic and medical evidence showed the "entirely preventable" deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.
The evidence did not support initial claims of a disease outbreak.
The detainees were found dead on 17 September while being held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on suspicion of illegal mining. The investigation found that the mining sites had been licensed.
'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria
Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said those found responsible for the deaths would face the full force of the law.
He added that the detention hall had been cleaned before investigators arrived, raising concerns about possible attempts to compromise evidence.
Implicated officers will face suspension and the report would be forwarded to the attorney general of the federation for further legal action, Tunji-Ojo said.
Family members reclaimed the bodies of their relatives from Minna's General Hospital last month
The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultation with the Mining Marshals Unit.
It said that 50 detainees had been held in a cell measuring about 20 sq m, with no running water or functioning toilet, and inadequate food, drinking water and airflow.
Adults and minors were detained together, and some detainees were held beyond lawful detention periods.
Officers reportedly ignored repeated calls for help, despite a medical worker having raised concerns about the conditions.
"Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance and pleaded for water," said the head of the investigating team, Jonathan Kure.
"These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties... but were not acted upon."
Kure said the detention conditions amounted to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment.
"The tragedy demonstrates the consequences of systemic disregard for detention standards, supervisory responsibilities and the welfare of persons in custody," he added.
The investigating committee also recommended compensation of 30m naira (Â£16,683; $22,285) for each of the bereaved families and 10m naira for each survivor.

articles.title_zh: iOS 27.2 has two CarPlay improvements, here’s what’s new
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.2 arrived this week with new features for Messages , Apple TV , and more, plus two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay users.
Apple Podcasts in iOS 27.2 adds two new sections to the Home tab: ‘New Episodes’ and ‘Continue Playing.’
Essentially, Apple has rethought how the core ‘Up Next’ queue of its Podcasts app works.
Like you would expect, ‘New Episodes’ contains only the latest episodes from your favorite shows. But after you’ve started an episode, you’ll find it in the ‘Continue Playing’ row just below.
This overhaul to podcast management makes it easier to find the latest episodes of your shows and also pick up where you previously left off. I’m a big fan of the change.
Siri AI introduces a variety of upgrades in iOS 27.2, including two that carry over to CarPlay as well.
Per Apple’s release notes :
It can take some adjustment to remember that Siri AI is available in the car just like on iPhone. But CarPlay is an especially useful platform for Apple’s more powerful assistant.

articles.title_orig: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
articles.title_zh: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
articles.content_orig:
Amazon laid out its AI usage guidelines for software engineers in a memo to staffers, and discouraged employees from turning to "tokenmaxxing" in their push to embrace artificial intelligence tools.
The memo , which was circulated internally in September and posted to the company's website on Tuesday, revises how the company defines the role of software development engineers and managers in the age of AI.
"We're just seeing the beginning of AI's effect on software engineering," the company wrote. "While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there's a lot that's still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice."
Under CEO Andy Jassy , Amazon has rapidly integrated AI across the company's sprawling business operations. Jassy has previously predicted that AI will "change the scope and speed" of day-to-day work, and potentially shrink its corporate workforce in the next few years through automation, though he's noted it will also create "other jobs."
As employees rush to adopt AI tools, companies have grappled with the technology's surging costs and how to reliably measure whether the technology leads to a productivity boost or other valuable returns on investment.
Companies have recently cracked down on tokenmaxxing , in which developers use AI as much as possible with little regard for output. Some companies have set limits on employees' usage of tokens, or the units of data that are processed and generated by AI models, in a bid to slow rising AI bills. Others have switched to cheaper, open-source models for certain tasks.
An Amazon spokesperson said the company hasn't instituted caps on employees' token usage. Amazon in May shut down an internal leaderboard after discovering employees were tokenmaxxing to climb the ranks.
In the memo posted Tuesday, Amazon said metrics like token usage, the rate of adoption of AI tools, and code changes or reviews remain "deeply flawed" ways of measuring teams or organizations' AI usage, adding that they can lead to higher costs and too much complexity.
It stopped short of telling staffers to ignore those metrics altogether, however. Token usage and code generation should be considered "with care and judgment" alongside other data, Amazon said.
"We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes," the company wrote.
Marc Brooker, a vice president and distinguished engineer at Amazon Web Services, told CNBC in an interview that the company has looked to metrics such as "feature velocity" to measure how AI is improving engineer productivity.
The metric looks at things like, "how many launches are we doing, how many successful changes are we making in production," he said.
"Broadly, we think about this as a return on investment," Brooker said. "If there is an important problem to solve for our customers, important problem to solve for our business, we're going to invest tools, time, tokens, human effort, etc. into those."
He added, "What we don't want to see is wasted effort where we are going and spending those tokens solving problems that don't matter and sometimes it's hard to know, so we do need to have some appetite for experimentation."
Amazon also discouraged staffers from using AI when it doesn't make sense for a given task.
"If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing," Amazon said in the memo.
The company added, "An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for."

articles.title_orig: Hasbro Appoints Dungeons & Dragons VP As Next President Of Wizards Of The Coast
articles.title_zh: Hasbro Appoints Dungeons & Dragons VP As Next President Of Wizards Of The Coast
articles.content_orig:
Wizards of the Coast, the company behind Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons , has been without a president for nearly two months. At the start of September, former president John Hight moved to an advisory role while Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks assumed oversight of Wizards of the Coast during the search for a new president. That search is finally over, and Dan Ayoub has been named the company's new president.
Hasbro announced the news in a news release on Oct. 27, revealing that Ayoub will become president of Wizards of the Coast and Hasbro Digital Games, effective Nov. 2. Ayoub most recently served as the senior vice president of D&D. He joined Wizards of the Coast in 2022 to lead the company's digital studios and also served as senior vice president of Digital Games, for a time. Before that, Ayoub also served as an executive producer and studio head at Halo developer 343 Industries.
Regarding his new position, Ayoub said this in an official statement:
“Magic and D&D have been part of my life for as long as I can remember, and the teams behind them are among the best in the world. We'll put fans first, respect the artists and creators who make these worlds come alive, and set an ambitious course for growth across tabletop and digital. I can't wait to get started.”
Given Ayoub's resume, it seems like Hasbro wants Wizards of the Coast to invest even more in digital and video games than it already does.
Hasbro already has Wizards of the Coast hard at work on several upcoming games. In light of recent news that Mass Effect studio BioWare has been shut down by EA, Exodus has attracted even more interest. The game is developed by Wizards of the Coast's division Archetype Entertainment, a developer studio headed by BioWare and Baldur's Gate series veteran James Ohlen. Exodus is one of two upcoming games (the other being The Expanse: Osiris Reborn ) positioned as spiritual successors to Mass Effect. Exodus is set to be a sprawling sci-fi RPG about exploring space and building relationships with companions. The game is slated for release on April 7, 2027.
More in line with what people might expect from Wizards of the Coast is Warlock , developed by Invoke Studios. Warlock is a single-player Dungeons & Dragons action-adventure game. The game sounds ambitious but also kind of gives Forspoken -vibes in gameplay footage we've seen so far. Warlock has a 2027 release window. Hasbro has also made it clear it wants to make a Baldur's Gate 4 eventually, though there are no hard plans for it at the moment.
